articles.title: Powertoys in Windows 11: Microsoft verpasst den Werkzeugen lokale KI
articles.text:
Windows 11: Update für Powertoys bringt neue Features und lokale KI
Die meisten Windows-11-User:innen werden nur die offensichtlichen Funktionen nutzen, die das Betriebssystem bereitstellt. Nur wenige dürften die sogenannten Powertoys kennen. Das Zusatzprogramm, das von Microsoft direkt angeboten wird, stellt zahlreiche zusätzliche Features für Windows 11 bereit, mit denen du das System weiter an deine Bedürfnisse anpassen kannst. Und jetzt steht dafür ein großes Update mit noch mehr Neuerungen bereit.
Windows 11: Was die Powertoys jetzt können
Zunächst verpasst Microsoft den Powertoys die lokale KI-Behandlung. Das „erweiterte Einfügen“ war schon vorab in der Lage, kopierte Inhalte über KI direkt beim Einfügen zu transformieren. So kann die KI etwa Texte aus Bildern extrahieren und dann einfügen. Jetzt vereinfacht Microsoft die Nutzung weiter, indem keinerlei API-Schlüssel oder Endpoints mehr für KI in der Cloud konfiguriert werden müssen. Stattdessen müssen Windows-11-User:innen nur einmalig das lokale KI-Modell Phi Silica herunterladen, das von Microsoft bereitgestellt wird.
Wurde das Modell installiert, läuft es komplett ohne Cloud-Anbindung auf dem Windows-PC und kann die Aufgaben des erweiterten Einfügens übernehmen. Microsoft betont, dass sich User:innen auch nicht nur auf ein Modell beschränken müssen. Sie können lokale und Cloud-Modelle frei miteinander kombinieren. Das ist besonders dann hilfreich, wenn ein Modell einen Arbeitsablauf besser versteht und erledigt als ein anderes.
Version 0.101 der Microsoft Powertoys führt zudem „Windows Hopper“ ein. Das Feature funktioniert ähnlich, wie die Alt-Tab unter Windows 11, allerdings verbleibt der Hopper dabei in einem ausgewählten Programm. Wer also schnell zwischen mehreren Datei-Explorer-Fenstern wählen will, statt durch alle anderen Apps zu switchen, kann so schneller zum Ziel gelangen.
Ebenfalls neu ist ein kompakter Modus der Befehlspalette. Über die Befehlszeile können Windows-User:innen Apps starten, Befehle ausführen und sogar Dateien und das Web durchsuchen. Zuvor machte die Befehlspalette schon vor Eingabe eines Buchstabens eine lange Liste an Vorschlägen, was die User:innen gebrauchen könnten. Um mehr Übersicht zu gewährleisten, startet die Befehlspalette mit der neuen Option als einzeiliges Kommando-Tool, das erst bei einer Eingabe relevante Vorschläge anzeigt.
Ferner können User:innen mit Powerdisplay jetzt die Helligkeit von mehreren angeschlossenen Bildschirmen gleichzeitig regeln. Ebenfalls spannend für künftige Releases ist, dass Microsoft einen Insider-Channel zu den Powertoys hinzufügt. Interessierte User:innen können sich dafür registrieren und bekommen so früheren Zugriff auf Neuerungen. Dafür müssen sie aber eventuell mit Problemen rechnen und sind dazu angehalten, Feedback an Microsoft zu senden, um die Bugs aus dem Weg zu räumen.

articles.title: Amazon, Flipkart restructure seller fees, penalties ahead of festival season
articles.text:
Amazon, Flipkart restructure seller fees, penalties ahead of festival season
Ecommerce giants Amazon and Flipkart have revised seller fees and penalty structures ahead of the festive shopping season, a move sellers say could further squeeze small and medium businesses already operating on thin margins.
Ecommerce majors Amazon and Flipkart have revised fee and penalty structures for sellers on their platforms in the weeks leading up to the festive shopping season, a move that sellers say adds to the financial burden on small and medium enterprises already operating on thin margins.
According to a notice issued by Amazon India on its seller forum, the company has, effective August 17, 2026, changed how it calculates order cancellation fees for sellers using its Easy Ship and Self Ship services.
Under Easy Ship, sellers store their own products, pack them when they receive an order and then hand them over to the Easy Ship Pickup executive, who then ships the product and ensures timely delivery.
In Self Ship, the seller packs and delivers the product themselves, using their own courier or delivery service, with no Amazon logistics involved.
The fee, previously based on category-specific referral charges, is now calculated as a percentage of the order value.
Under the revised structure, sellers are charged 10% of the order value for orders below Rs 10,000, 8% for orders between Rs 10,001 and Rs 50,000, 5% for orders between Rs 50,001 and Rs 1,00,000, and 2% for orders above Rs 1,00,000, with an 18% goods and services tax levied in addition.
The fee applies when a seller cancels an order for reasons other than a buyer's request and when an order is automatically cancelled because the seller does not ship and confirm the shipment within 24 hours of the estimated ship date.
In another notice, Amazon said it will increase closing fees across its Fulfilment Center, Easy Ship, and Seller Flex channels with effect from September 7, 2026.
Amazon charges a closing fee every time a product is sold, based on the product's price range. This fee varies based on the fulfilment channel a seller is using.
The fee will rise by Rs 1 for products priced up to Rs 500 and by Rs 3 for products priced above Rs 500. The company attributed the increase to higher fuel and logistics costs.
"We expect orders placed by customers to be fulfilled reliably by sellers on our marketplace. To encourage timely and dependable fulfilment, we have revised cancellation fees for Easy Ship and Self-Ship sellers. This fee is conditional and only applies in the rare event of a seller-initiated cancellation, which accounts for less than 1 per cent of orders on Amazon.in. We have appropriate measures in place to ensure sellers are protected when cancellations are due to circumstances beyond their control," an Amazon spokesperson said.
Responding to notices on Amazon's seller forum, some sellers said cancellations were at times caused by factors outside their control, such as delivery personnel failing to arrive for a scheduled pickup, and questioned why cancellation fees should apply to the seller in such instances.
Another seller said the difference in total fees between sellers using Amazon's fulfilment network and those on Easy Ship could be as high as Rs 45 per unit on comparable orders, which the seller said creates an unfair competitive situation.
Flipkart, meanwhile, has put in place a three-tier penalty structure for order-fulfilment lapses, effective August 23, 2026.
Under this structure, a shipment not made ready for pickup by the committed Dispatch By Date (DBD) attracts a fine of Rs 30 per shipment. An order cancelled by the seller, or automatically cancelled after three missed dispatch deadlines, attracts a fine of Rs 60 per shipment. Where an order is both delayed and subsequently cancelled, the penalty rises to Rs 90 per shipment.
Under the earlier regime, a DBD breach could lock the seller's account for a period of time, which had a greater impact on the seller's business.
New sellers on Flipkart, up to three months into their selling journey, will not be impacted by this policy.
The new structure aimed to inculcate better seller behaviour and encourage sellers to plan better, with the objective of improving customer experience, people aware of the development told PTI.
They said sellers were also rewarded for maintaining good DBD compliance, with benefits such as faster payment settlement and complimentary advertising credits.
Vinod Kumar, Trustee of the Forum for Internet Resellers, Sellers and Traders (FIRST INDIA), said Indian online sellers recognise the need for timely fulfilment and high customer service standards, but the recent increase in cancellation, dispatch and other seller penalties by major ecommerce marketplaces, particularly ahead of the festive season, was a matter of concern for MSMEs already facing thin margins and rising costs.
Kumar said not every cancellation or delay was caused by the seller, citing logistics failures, platform issues, demand spikes and customer-related factors as other possible causes.
"Sellers should not become the default financial shock absorbers of the e-commerce ecosystem.
"Marketplaces must ensure transparent attribution of responsibility, reasonable and proportionate penalties, adequate advance notice of fee changes and a simple mechanism to challenge wrongful charges. The objective should be to improve fulfilment while making digital commerce more, not less, viable for small businesses," Kumar added.

articles.title: AnonyMousKIT PhaaS uses voice AI agents to phish iPhone passcodes
articles.text:
A newly uncovered phishing-as-a-service (PhaaS) platform called AnonyMousKIT automates the retrieval of codes used to unlock stolen Apple devices and disable the Activation Lock feature.
The illegal service has been active since early 2024 and is powering a structured ecosystem that sells stolen iPhones, harvests Apple IDs, accesses iCloud backups, and Keychain credentials.
Researchers at threat intelligence platform SOCRadar took advantage of the platform operator's use of bare relative paths to gather information on how the service works, its operators, and infrastructure.
SOCRadar found that AnonyMousKIT is connected to 506 domains and is fueling a sprawling business with 168 storefront brands acting as resellers.
The researchers recovered records of 200 calls made to victims between August 2025 and May 2026, using 55 distinct interaction transcripts handled by a voice AI agent operating under five personas.
SOCRadar notes that the calls cost the operator about $0.10 per attempt, adding that 90% of the calls were made to Brazil.
Retrieving unlocking codes
Apple's Activation Lock feature activates automatically when the Find My tracking service is turned on, and links the iPhone device to the owner’s Apple Account.
Even if a stolen device is factory-reset, it remains linked to the original owner's account and requires a valid authorization code during first setup before it can be used.
Because of this protection feature, many stolen iPhones are sold for parts. However, their value increases significantly if they can be unlocked, especially when sensitive data belonging to the owner can also be recovered.
AnonyMousKIT retrieves information from stolen devices, such as the owner’s contact information supplied through the Lost Mode feature, and uses it to contact the owner through email, SMS, WhatsApp, or a phone call.
The phishing messages impersonate Apple and claim that the missing device has been located, providing the correct model and IMEI details to make the email appear legitimate.
The email takes the victim to a fake Find My or Apple page where they are prompted to enter their device passcode, Apple Account credentials, and the two-factor authentication code.
In some cases examined by SOCRadar, an AI agent with an “Alice from Apple Support” persona informs victims that someone trying to unlock the phone brought it to an Apple store, where the device was retained.
The AI agent then asks the victim to confirm ownership by dictating the passcode, then directs them to the phishing page.
Once the threat actors obtain those codes, they can access the victim's personal data, factory reset the device, and remove it from the Find My app before selling it.
A compromised Apple ID could expose iCloud backups, Keychain passwords, work email, and other corporate information stored on personal or employer-issued Apple devices, SOCRadar warns.
The researchers found that a small percentage of the emails from the platform were sent to government and corporate organizations.
SOCRadar reports that the campaigns facilitated by the AnonuMousKIT had a global footprint, but were more concentrated in South Africa, Indonesia, Italy, India, Kenya, and Brazil.
Once attackers have valid credentials, only 37% of their actions are blocked
Overall prevention scores can hide what happens after initial access. Once attackers are using valid credentials, prevention drops sharply.

articles.title: MTN has 5 million fintech users in Nigeria. It wants 30 million.
articles.text:
MTN, Africa’s largest telecoms group, has built one of the continent’s biggest mobile-money businesses. But with far more telecom customers than MoMo users, it has a huge opportunity to turn its network into a fintech growth engine.
That opportunity is most pronounced in Nigeria, where the telecom giant has five million fintech customers but sees a path to as many as 30 million over the medium term. The company is now bringing in technology from Alibaba, a technology and commerce giant, Alipay, a Chinese digital payments platform, and Ant International Group. It is also preparing to move deeper into lending, including using its own balance sheet.
Speaking to TechCabal a day after MTN released its six-month financial results, group CEO Ralph Mupita said Nigeria remains a key market for expanding the company’s fintech business. “It would be converting more of the Nigerian customers who are using our telecommunications services into fintech customers,” he said.
Mupita stated that getting that ratio to 30%, or potentially 50%, would translate into around 30 million customers. “Can we grow from 5 million to 30 million customers over the medium term? If we did that, I guess we would be able to say to you in the medium term that we’ve been successful,” he noted.
The ambition comes as MTN’s fintech business is already operating at significant scale across Africa. In the six months ended June, MoMo monthly active users rose 12.1% to 70.8 million, while fintech transaction volumes increased 17.2% to 13 billion. Transaction value rose 33.8% in constant currency to $330.5 billion.
But the gap between MTN’s telecom and fintech customer bases highlights the challenge the business faces. Having hundreds of millions of mobile customers does not automatically mean those customers will use payments, lending, insurance or other financial products.
According to Mupita, MTN is looking beyond simply adding more MoMo users. In Nigeria, it is using technology from Alibaba, Alipay and Ant International as it tries to build out its fintech proposition and compete in a market already crowded with digital financial-services companies such as OPay and PalmPay.
“There are many fintech businesses there (Nigeria), MoneyPoint, OPay, PalmPay and others, but there is room for quite a lot of players, and we see a lot of growth there,” Mupita told TechCabal.
The strategy also points to a bigger change in what MTN wants its fintech business to become. The company is moving beyond payments and into lending, which Mupita described as the major future opportunity in advanced financial services. The International Finance Corporation (IFC) estimates the micro, small and medium enterprises financing gap in Sub-Saharan Africa at $331 billion, including $32.2 billion in Nigeria alone.
The Group currently works with commercial partner banks that use its customer data to assess whether customers qualify for credit, but Mupita said the company intends to look internally. “But increasingly, you’re going to see us lending off our own balance sheet,” he stated.
That would mark a significant evolution for a telecom operator whose financial-services business has historically been built around payments and partnerships with banks. It also introduces a new set of risks, particularly credit risk, as MTN takes greater responsibility for loans issued through its ecosystem.
Mupita acknowledged that evolution: “That’s something we’re going to do incrementally because, obviously, it comes with risk.”
MTN’s latest results show that fintech growth is coming from a portfolio of markets, with Nigeria and Ghana among the strongest contributors, while Côte d’Ivoire, Cameroon, Uganda and Rwanda are also adding momentum. The group said its broader portfolio helped offset temporary challenges in individual markets.
Mupita added that the company also has a growing merchant network to support the expansion. It ended the period with 2.3 million merchants, while advanced services, including lending, payments, remittances and insurance, grew 31.8% in constant currency.
That makes the 30 million-customer target less about launching another standalone fintech product and more about exploiting an asset MTN already owns: its massive telecom distribution network.
True scale demands moving beyond surface-level integrations to robust execution. articles.title: Yang Zhilin tenía Silicon Valley a sus pies: prefirió regresar a China y construir una de las IA más impresionantes del mundo
articles.text:
Yang Zhilin es uno de los científicos expertos en inteligencia artificial (IA) más importantes de China. Ahora mismo es razonable incluso considerarlo el más relevante de esta nación asiática debido a que es el principal responsable de Kimi K3, la IA china que ha conseguido pelear de tú a tú con los modelos más avanzados de OpenAI o Anthropic. La historia de Zhilin está marcada por el éxito desde el principio, pero lo que a menudo se pasa por alto es que las grandes tecnológicas estadounidenses pelearon entre ellas para ficharlo.
Unos apuntes biográficos breves para meternos en harina. Yang Zhilin, de 34 años, nació en Shantou, provincia de Guangdong (China), y se formó en Ciencias de la Computación en la prestigiosa Universidad de Tsinghua, en Pekín, un centro de enseñanza e investigación considerado "el MIT chino". Cuando concluyó su licenciatura decidió complementar su formación en EEUU, así que consiguió que lo aceptasen en un programa de doctorado en la Universidad Carnegie Mellon, en Pittsburgh (Pensilvania).
Durante sus años de formación en China, Zhilin exploró varias áreas de la informática, como la teoría de grafos o el aprendizaje multimodal, pero no se volcó definitivamente en la IA hasta que sus mentores en Carnegie Mellon, Ruslan Salakhutdinov (excientífico jefe de IA en Apple) y William Cohen, le animaron a focalizar su esfuerzo en los modelos de lenguaje. Este es el momento en el que su historia se pone realmente interesante. Y es que Zhilin fue uno de los artífices de Transformer-XL y XLNet, las dos arquitecturas de procesamiento del lenguaje natural que han desencadenado la explosión de la IA que estamos viviendo.
De Transformer-XL a Kimi K3
Los transformers de los que con tanta frecuencia oímos hablar en el ámbito de la IA son una arquitectura diseñada para conseguir que una máquina pueda entender las relaciones que existen entre las palabras o las diferentes partes de una información. Su propósito es identificar cuáles son realmente importantes para interpretar el conjunto de los datos que están siendo procesados. Los transformers fueron desarrollados por varios investigadores de Google, entre los que se encuentran Ashish Vaswani, Noam Shazeer, Niki Parmar o Łukasz Kaiser, entre otros.
El corazón de los transformers es el mecanismo de atención, que, muy a grandes rasgos, permite a un modelo identificar qué palabras de una frase debe evaluar para comprender qué relaciones existen entre ellas y cuál es el significado de cada una de ellas, así como del conjunto. El problema de esta estrategia es que el contexto de los transformers estaba limitado a una ventana de tokens, por lo que cuando el modelo procesaba un nuevo fragmento de texto estaba restringido por la imposibilidad de acceder a la información que había quedado fuera de esa ventana.
El mecanismo de atención permite a un modelo identificar qué palabras de una frase debe evaluar para comprender qué relaciones existen entre ellas
Yang Zhilin y varios de sus colegas en Carnegie Mellon resolvieron esta limitación de un plumazo proponiendo una especie de memoria entre segmentos con Transformer-XL. Y poco después junto a otros colaboradores desarrolló XLNet, una arquitectura que permite a un modelo predecir palabras a partir de diferentes órdenes de permutación. Estos dos trabajos fueron fundamentales en el desarrollo de la IA tal y como la conocemos, por lo que Zhilin pudo hacer estancias para seguir investigando en Google Brain y Meta, y cuando acabó su doctorado las grandes tecnológicas estadounidenses se lo rifaron.
Pero Zhilin no tenía intención de quedarse en EEUU. Había viajado allí para completar su formación, y una vez que la dio por concluida decidió regresar a China con el propósito de fundar su propia empresa de IA. Fue exactamente lo que hizo. Nada más regresar a China participó en dos proyectos nacionales esenciales: PanGu, de Huawei, y WuDao, de la Academia de Inteligencia Artificial de Pekín. Y en marzo de 2023 cofundó Moonshot AI junto a dos de sus antiguos compañeros en la Universidad de Tsinghua.
El resto es historia. En julio de 2026 Moonshot AI lanzó Kimi K3, un modelo de IA de 2,8 billones de parámetros con pesos abiertos y capaz de competir con los principales modelos cerrados de EEUU, como Claude Opus 4.8 de Anthropic o GPT-5.5 de OpenAI, quedando solo por detrás de los más recientes Claude Fable 5 y GPT-5.6 Sol. Zhilin ha sido utilizado por algunos inversores estadounidenses como el símbolo del debate sobre la fuga de talento en EEUU propiciada por la política migratoria de la Administración Trump, que, según ellos, está empujando a los mejores cerebros de vuelta a China.

articles.title: Bloqué en France, Polymarket contre-attaque : le site de paris crypto saisit la justice, mais mise sur le dialogue
articles.text:
Cet été, l’Autorité nationale des jeux (ANJ) a ordonné le blocage complet de Polymarket en France. Déjà mise en demeure en 2024, la controversée plateforme de paris en cryptomonnaies a été bloquée par les FAI. Selon l’autorité française, le site développé par une société panaméenne « fait la promotion d’une offre illégale de jeux d’argent et de hasard » et rappelle que « les sites de prédiction ne sont pas autorisés en France et qu’ils sont considérés comme des sites de jeux d’argent illégaux et exposent donc leurs utilisateurs à de nombreux risques (addiction, intégrité, etc.) ». La France rejoint ainsi une douzaine de pays européens ayant déjà restreint Polymarket, dont l’Allemagne, la Belgique et l’Italie.
À lire aussi : Une fuite massive de données met en danger 13 000 détenteurs de cryptomonnaies
Polymarket conteste son blocage en France
Quelques semaines après le blocage ordonné par l’Autorité nationale des jeux (ANJ), Polymarket passe à la contre-attaque. La plateforme révèle avoir saisi la justice pour contester la décision prise par l’ANJ le mois dernier, tout en tentant d’ouvrir le dialogue avec la France. Polymarket accuse l’ANJ d’avoir pris une mesure « unilatérale », coupant l’accès à son service aux utilisateurs français et francophones.
La plateforme insiste sur la valeur de ses marchés prédictifs, capables selon elle de refléter le sentiment public et les tendances géopolitiques, bien au-delà du simple pari spéculatif. La plateforme parle d’un « recours auprès des autorités compétentes en France », mais ne précise pas quelles actions précises ont été engagées.
« Bien que nous soyons en désaccord avec la décision de l’autorité de régulation des jeux, la France a fait preuve d’un engagement fort en faveur de l’innovation financière et technologique, et nos récentes discussions avec les autorités françaises ont été constructives et encourageantes », indique Polymarket dans un communiqué de presse.
Un dialogue qui se veut constructif
Sous l’impulsion d’Emmanuel Macron, l’Hexagone a attiré avec succès plusieurs géants des cryptomonnaies sur son territoire par le passé, dont Binance, Crypto.com, Circle ou encore OKX. Ces entités ont ouvert un siège social à Paris. Polymarket semble vouloir s’appuyer sur la stratégie du gouvernement français à l’égard de l’industrie crypto pour tenter d’éviter un blocage et « maintenir un dialogue constructif avec l’ANJ ». Le site « continue de dialoguer avec les autorités françaises et reste déterminé à opérer de manière à répondre aux attentes réglementaires applicables tout en préservant les avantages des marchés de prédiction pour ses utilisateurs », conclut le communiqué.

articles.title: Black Hat State of Security Vendors - Schneier on Security
articles.text:
Black Hat State of Security Vendors
Andy Ellis has a roundup of the security vendors at Black Hat this year.
Key Takeaways: We have entered into an AI world. While nearly half of booths didn’t directly mention AI or agents in their taglines, the effects of AI are everywhere. Multiple spaces (Identity, SaaS, AppSec, Data) have almost every vendor leading with AI; existing unsolved problem areas just got worse.
At the same time, there’s a clear trichotomy in the market: tools that tell you how bad things are; tools that stop adversaries, and tools that prevent problems from occurring. While you’d suspect that the tools that fix things would dominate, the tools that merely tell you how bad things are seem to be frustratingly plentiful.
For Profit • August 25, 2026 7:29 AM
Of course there’s dominance by tools that say how bad things are, that’s to motivate people to buy the tools that fix things. It’s a marketing strategy, IMHO.

articles.title: The Witcher 4 Gets 2028 Release Window but No Gamescom Gameplay Preview
articles.text:
Tuesday, August 25th 2026
	
	
	
	
The Witcher 4 Gets 2028 Release Window but No Gamescom Gameplay Preview
It's now been over a year since CD Projekt Red, the game studio behind the Witcher franchise, revealed that The Witcher 4 would likely launch "after 2026." Now, in a recent announcement, CD Projekt Red revealed that it would be showing off The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt—Songs of the Past at Gamescom opening night, but that The Witcher 4 would not be making an appearance. 
As Michał Nowakowski, joint-CEO of CDPR, explains in an X post and a YouTube video embedded below, The Witcher 4 is the studio's "biggest, boldest, and most ambitious game to date," and it has over 500 developers and artists working on the game. He adds that an exact launch date for The Witcher 4 has not been decided just yet, but the studio can confirm that the game will launch at some point in 2028.The 2028 release window is simply the game's target release window, implying that even that is not a fixed point, but The Witcher 4 has been in full-scale development since late 2024, and the game studio has said that it has revamped its development processes following the less-than-satisfactory launch of Cyberpunk 2077. The co-CEO also confirmed that The Witcher 4 would show up at Gamescom events in the coming years, suggesting we will likely see a gameplay reveal or demo at Gamescom 2027 or 2028.

articles.title: New bootloader lets you take the "Meta" out of the original Meta Quest
articles.text:
Remember the original Quest headset that Meta (then Oculus) trumpeted back in 2019? Meta seems to hope you don’t, since the company officially stopped supporting the wireless VR headset in 2023 to focus on the more popular Quests 2 and 3. However, tinkerers haven’t abandoned the hardware and recently released a new root-access exploit and bootloader that gives “developers and enthusiasts full control over Quest 1 hardware.”
The QuestStack project integrates previously known vulnerabilities in the Quest’s Android fastboot process into a privilege escalation chain that leads easily to full root access on the device. The bootloading process is now streamlined enough that it can be completed without any downloads through a web interface after connecting the headset to a PC.
With this exploit, the original Quest hardware can now be officially divorced from any reliance on Meta’s servers or services to be useful. That means enterprising Quest owners should be able to sideload apps without needing to register for a Meta Developer account and activating Developer Mode through Meta’s mobile app. It also means users should be able to go through the initial setup and login steps for a fresh Quest headset even if and when Meta decides to shut down the servers that currently support this process.

articles.title: Russian tech giant VK wants Apple to pay $696,000 every day until its apps return to the App Store
articles.text:
What just happened? Not for the first time, Russia is suing a US firm for a very large sum of money – though the lawsuit on this occasion comes from a company rather than its government. The $696,000 that VK wants from Apple for blocking its apps might not seem like a lot to the tech giant, but VK is asking for that amount every day. That would come to around $21 million per month, or $252 million per year.
VK, which was known as Mail.ru Group until 2021, filed the suit against Apple in a Moscow arbitration court after the US firm removed its apps from the App Store in June.
Apple removed several VK apps, including VKontakte, VK Messenger, VK Video, Zen, Mail Cloud, Mail, Skillbox, and Youla. Cupertino said it removed them to comply with EU sanctions imposed on VK and its subsidiary, Communication Platform LLC. The apps have also been removed from the Google Play Store.
The EU said the companies were involved in activities that enabled citizen surveillance, censorship, and the identification of individuals opposed to Russian government policies.
VK is asking the court to order Apple to restore its apps to the store. If it fails to comply, VK is requesting 50 million rubles, about $600,000 per day, for the continued blocking of its flagship VKontakte app, 5 million rubles, about $60,000, for VK Music, and 3 million rubles, around $36,000, for Odnoklassniki. If Apple does not comply, the company wants the daily fines to begin on the sixth day after the court issues its ruling.
VK wants the penalties imposed on Russia-based Apple Rus LLC, US-based Apple Inc., and Ireland-based Apple Distribution International Ltd.
The Kremlin said Apple's decision to remove the apps called into question the company's "reliability as a provider of commercial services."
Russia has a long history of taking Western technology companies to court, though many of the cases have involved government regulators imposing fines rather than Russian companies filing lawsuits.
Google has been the most prominent target. In 2022, a Russian court fined the company $373 million for failing to remove prohibited YouTube videos. Its Russian subsidiary subsequently filed for bankruptcy after authorities seized its bank account.
The most extreme example came in 2024, when 17 Russian television channels sued Google over YouTube blocking their accounts. Daily penalties that doubled every week eventually reached a hilarious $20.5 decillion, more than the value of the entire global economy. Russian media companies sought to enforce the rulings in Turkey, Hungary, Spain, South Africa, and other countries, but Google said it didn't expect the Russian legal proceedings to have a material effect on its business.
Russia has also filed a case against Meta, resulting in Facebook and Instagram being declared "extremist" and banned from operating in the country. Its courts and regulators have imposed penalties on Airbnb, Pinterest, Twitch, UPS, WhatsApp, Facebook, and Twitter over data-storage rules, while Reddit, Apple, and the Wikimedia Foundation have been fined for refusing to remove content deemed illegal by Moscow.
Russia has often struggled to collect its largest and most headline-grabbing penalties, especially after Western companies withdrew from the country and local subsidiaries were closed or driven into bankruptcy. But Apple is a notable exception: in 2024, it paid a $13.65 million App Store antitrust fine, having previously paid another $12.12 million penalty. Whether VK will have similar success collecting hundreds of millions of dollars in accumulating daily fines remains to be seen.

articles.title: No todo es IA: NVIDIA RTX Spark llevará los mejores juegos a Windows en ARM
articles.text:
NVIDIA presentó RTX Spark a principios de junio, con la promesa de revolucionar la experiencia de Windows en ARM. El superchip de la compañía se ha desarrollado pensando especialmente en las labores de IA, pero también va a desbloquear una nueva era para los fanáticos del gaming.
En el marco de la Gamescom 2026, NVIDIA anunció que los principales estudios van a llevar sus mejores juegos y sus tecnologías antitrampa a RTX Spark. Si bien previamente se sabía que empresas como Riot Games, Xbox y Krafton iban a soportar el hardware en cuestión, ahora se están sumando firmas del calibre de Electronic Arts, Ubisoft y Embark Studios.
El caso de EA es de los más resonantes, puesto que va a brindar soporte para la tecnología antitrampas Javelin en RTX Spark. Esto significa que títulos muy populares en el mundo de los eSports, como Apex Legends y F1 25, se podrán jugar desde los dispositivos impulsados por el nuevo chip de NVIDIA.
Otros títulos con muchos seguidores que llegarán a RTX Spark son The Finals y el shooter de extracción ARC Raiders. En tanto que Ubisoft ha prometido incorporar el juego de estrategias Anno 117: Pax Romana al catálogo de juegos soportados por el hardware de NVIDIA.
El siguiente vídeo de NVIDIA permite ver títulos como Cyberpunk 2077: Ultimate Edition, Alan Wake II y Pragmata ejecutándose en RTX Spark.
NVIDIA quiere que RTX Spark sea una plataforma de gaming
Windows en ARM es una plataforma que ha prometido mucho, pero que hasta aquí nunca ha despegado. RTX Spark busca darle el impulso necesario a la plataforma, y el gaming puede jugar un papel crucial para que ello ocurra. Claro que para ello necesita de un compromiso permanente de los estudios para adaptar, mantener y expandir su catálogo de títulos.
NVIDIA va a mostrar las cualidades de RTX Spark como plataforma de videojuegos durante la Gamescom 2026, con múltiples demos en su sector de exposición. Los primeros portátiles impulsados por el superchip de la compañía estarán disponibles durante el otoño, aunque todavía no hay una fecha confirmada en tal sentido.
Como ya dijimos, el gigante verde tiene el apoyo de múltiples pesos pesados de la industria para avanzar con esta apuesta. Además de EA, Ubisoft, Krafton o Riot Games, la iniciativa también tiene el aval de SEGA, Capcom, Epic Games, KONAMI y CD Projekt RED, por solo nombrar algunos.
Si bien RTX Spark aspira a abrir una nueva etapa en el mundo de los "ordenadores agénticos" gracias a su enfoque en la inteligencia artificial, se juega puntos importantes en la búsqueda de contentar a los gamers, un público siempre exigente. Según NVIDIA, su nuevo hardware permitirá jugar en 1440p a 100 cuadros por segundo, con ray tracing y DLSS.

articles.title: Life360 expands pet tracking with new $8 scannable tags and zoomie alerts | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Family location-sharing and safety app Life360 is expanding its pet-tracking capabilities on Tuesday with the launch of a new product line of $7.99 scannable pet tags and other pet-care features that tap into its tracking network technology.
Life360 expanded into pet tech last year with the launch of GPS pet trackers that leverage the lost-item-finding capabilities that the company integrated into its platform after its 2021 acquisition of AirTag rival Tile. With Tile, the company now offers not just location-sharing features for families, but also the ability for members to track other things of importance — like keys, handbags, luggage, and pets.
Since then, families on the service have added more than 8 million pets to their accounts, the company says.
However, the team found that not everyone wants to attach a bulky tracker to their pet’s collar, and not everyone needs access to location-tracking features or other advanced options like geofences and escape alerts.
In many cases, pet owners just want to put their contact information on a pet’s tag, which is what the new scannable pet tags support.
But there’s a twist. Instead of just providing a pet owner’s phone number when someone scans the QR code printed on the new pet tags, the scan also alerts the family through the Life360 app installed on the family’s smartphones. (The person who found the pet does not need to have the app for this to work.)
This helps in multiple ways — not only does it provide peace of mind to families searching for a lost pet, but it also provides the pet’s location details. That can be useful if the lost pet escapes from the finder’s control and runs off again, as the family will at least have the last known location recorded.
Families can update their contact details through the Life360 pet profile in the app.
In addition, the company is rolling out several new pet-care features for families, including tools that let families schedule “care logs” to manage and track whether the pet has been fed, walked, given medication, or had its litter cleaned. Everyone in the family can see these care routines, so they will know if the pet needs their attention.
Another fun feature is “Zoomies Alerts” for GPS trackers, which track the bursts of energy a pet has at particular points during the day or evening. A new Weekly Roundup will recap other routines, like the distance walked or information about who in the family provided the pet with the most care during the week.
With the new features, the company is also making its pet trackers more affordable. Before, the Pet GPS trackers were only available with the higher-tier Platinum and Gold subscriptions, but now they’re included with the $99-per-year Silver bundles, too.
The new pet tags and GPS trackers are sold on both the company’s website and Amazon in the U.S., Canada, Australia, New Zealand, and the U.K.

articles.title: Garmin’s new Fenix 9 adds brighter screens and smoother map panning
articles.text:
Garmin just took the wraps off its new line of rugged Fenix 9 smartwatches, with the base model featuring an OLED display with a brightness of up to 3,000 nits, making it twice as bright as its predecessor. Starting at $999.99 for the 43mm case option, the Fenix 9 has 50 percent more RAM and an upgraded map engine, allowing for faster panning.
Garmin’s new Fenix 9 adds brighter screens and smoother map panning
The Fenix 9 and 9 Pro come equipped with an OLED display with up to 3,000 nits of brightness.
It also comes with a scratch-resistant sapphire lens, an increased 64GB of storage, and a bunch of new software-based features, like Garmin Epic. This feature groups all the workouts you’ve done over several days, weeks, or months to create an “Epic” that shows your health and performance data within that period. There are also new stamina tracking metrics and expanded rucking features that let you change the weight of your pack during a workout. Garmin says the Fenix 9 offers up to 29 days of battery life in smartwatch mode on the largest 51mm size.
The Fenix 9 Pro starts at $1,099.99 and expands on these upgrades with a new titanium case. It has InReach satellite or LTE connectivity available on all three 43mm, 47mm, and 51mm options for an extra $100 and a $7.99 / month subscription. The largest Fenix 9 Pro variation also offers a 1.5-inch OLED display for the first time. That’s just a little bigger than the 1.3-inch and 1.4-inch displays available with the smaller case sizes across the Fenix 9 lineup.
Additionally, the 47mm and 51mm Fenix 9 Pro models offer a solar-charged display option that promises up to 57 days of battery life (with the caveat that you spend three hours per day outside in 50,000 lux conditions).
The Fenix 9 lineup is available in an array of case and band color combinations. The new devices will be available to order starting August 28th.

articles.title: TSMC’s HBM-Packaging Yield Issues Help Intel, Analysts Say - EE Times
articles.text:
TSMC’s difficulty stitching together AI accelerators with high-bandwidth memory (HBM) on a single chip gives Intel a chance to win foundry customers, according to Counterpoint Research co-founder Neil Shah and other analysts commenting to EE Times.
TSMC’s CoWoS advanced packaging tech, which has been a mainstay for AI customers like Nvidia, AMD, and Broadcom for years, has become a production bottleneck, Shah said in an Aug. 17 report he provided to EE Times.
“HBM’s reliance on TSMC’s CoWoS silicon interposers carries steep costs with thick packages, yield risk, capacity constraints and high scrap costs, thus creating an opening for credible alternatives,” Shah said. Intel’s EMIB advanced packaging that’s in production, as well as the company’s longer-term solutions like Z-angle memory (ZAM) and cross-batch memory (XBM), can help eliminate TSMC’s interposer problem for AI chipmakers, Shah added.
“Large silicon dies have high defect rates. If the interposer fails during final packaging, the GPU die and all eight or more attached HBM stacks are ruined,” Shah said. “Scrapping an assembled package because of an interconnect or interposer defect destroys thousands of dollars in silicon at the final step.”
Building strength
Other analysts agreed that Intel is building strength.
“Intel already has a number of important external customers for packaging with good growth potential over the next few years,” International Business Strategies CEO Handel Jones told EE Times. “Intel has good technology in packaging and is expanding capacity including in Santa Fe, New Mexico.”
Jones declined to identify Intel Foundry customers, citing confidentiality agreements with clients.
Intel’s EMIB is proven in high-volume products like the company’s Sapphire Rapids and Ponte Vecchio processors, as well as custom accelerator designs, Shah said.
Counterpoint said its channel checks suggest Google and AI ASIC design partner MediaTek will use Intel Foundry’s EMIB-T for Google’s upcoming TPUv9t (Humufish), TPUv9t+ (Triggerfish), and beyond.
Intel still faces hurdles, according to Counterpoint.
“TSMC and HBM remains the safest, most flexible generalist platform for simultaneous training
and inference,” Shah said. “Nvidia and AMD have so far showed no inclination to diversify. At the same time, we see Google [with MediaTek] looking to diversify, which would be huge as it [Google] is the second largest accelerator company in the world.”
In May, the Wall Street Journal reported that Apple may order chips from Intel, a deal prompted by U.S. President Donald Trump. The Trump administration took a 10% stake in Intel last year.
Packaging
Advanced packaging has extended the benefits of Moore’s Law by allowing multiple dies and chiplets to be integrated into increasingly dense packages. Nvidia’s latest AI chips integrate hundreds of billions of transistors across two compute dies in a single package.
From a performance and power-consumption perspective, enhancements in packaging tech will be more important than the migration of leading foundries like TSMC and Intel from 2.0-nm to 1.4-nm chip processes, Jones said.
Intel’s chance depends on timely execution and support from companies like Google and MediaTek as well as Tier-1 memory players, Counterpoint said.
Intel’s EMIB, together with ZAM and XBM, will be factors behind the transition, according to the research firm.
In February, Intel and SoftBank subsidiary Saimemory announced ZAM, a stacked DRAM technology. ZAM would serve as an energy-efficient alternative to HBM. In the longer term, XBM would use back-end-of-line (BEOL) thin-film transistors and serial UCIe links to eliminate interposers.
Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan recently telegraphed memory’s increasing importance to the company.
Staying competitive
TSMC is enhancing CoWoS to stay competitive, Counterpoint said.
CoWoS-L is architecturally similar to EMIB, using small, localized silicon bridges for high-density die-to-die routing, the Counterpoint report noted. Intel embeds an EMIB bridge directly inside an organic substrate cavity while TSMC embeds the integration bridge into an intermediate redistribution layer (RDL) in a silicon wafer layer before attaching it to a substrate, the report said.
“I’m inclined to believe TSMC has excellent yields for its CoWoS processes,” analyst Mike Demler told EE Times. “The newer CoWos-L may have had some early yield issues, and there were reports of some delays with [Nvidia’s] Vera Rubin, but I’m not aware of any current yield issues.”
Intel’s chance to take AI chip customers away from TSMC looks good, Demler said.
“EMIB eliminates the interposer, and Foveros [Intel’s 3D chip-stacking tech] offers die-stacking and other features TSMC doesn’t have,” he said. “If nothing else, Intel has an opportunity to pick up customers because of TSMC’s capacity shortage.”
TSMC and Intel didn’t respond to EE Times before publication of this article.

articles.title: Why a Robot Vacuum Changes the Way You Keep Your Home Clean - Tech Guide
articles.text:
There is a particular kind of frustration that comes from vacuuming a floor and watching it look dirty again within hours — pet hair drifting back across hardwood, crumbs reappearing under the kitchen table, dust settling on a rug you just cleaned.
The traditional vacuum demands your time, your effort, and your presence, and it only makes a difference for a short window before entropy reasserts itself. A robot vacuum works on a fundamentally different logic: it cleans frequently and automatically, so floors stay in good condition between the deeper cleans rather than steadily deteriorating until cleaning becomes an unavoidable chore.
The technology behind these devices has matured substantially. Early robot vacuums bumped into furniture, got stuck on rugs, and missed half the floor. Modern units use lidar or camera-based mapping to build a precise floor plan, navigate methodically, and avoid obstacles with impressive accuracy. Self-emptying dock stations mean some users go weeks without directly touching the robot or its dust bin. If you’ve been on the fence about whether a robot vacuum is worth the investment, this guide breaks down how they work, what to prioritise when buying, and how to get the most out of one in a real home.
How Modern Robot Vacuums Actually Navigate
Navigation technology is where the gap between budget and mid-to-premium robot vacuums is most pronounced. Entry-level models use random-bounce navigation: the robot moves in a straight line until it hits something, then turns at an angle and continues. This approach eventually covers most of the floor, but it’s inefficient, takes longer, and leaves gaps — especially in corners and along edges. It also means the robot can’t build a map of your home, so it can’t be directed to clean a specific room or avoid a specific area.
Lidar-based navigation uses a spinning laser sensor on top of the robot to measure the distance to surrounding objects several hundred times per second. This data is used to build a real-time map of the space, allowing the robot to plot an efficient, systematic cleaning path rather than wandering. The resulting maps are saved to the app, where you can label rooms, set virtual boundaries, and schedule specific zones for cleaning at different times. Camera-based navigation works similarly but uses visual landmarks instead of laser ranging — it’s generally less reliable in low-light environments but allows the front-facing camera to also function as an obstacle detection system.
Obstacle Avoidance and Its Real-World Limits
Obstacle avoidance is one of the most actively marketed features in this category, and the quality varies significantly. Basic obstacle detection stops the robot before it collides with a chair leg or a shoe; advanced systems using structured-light 3D sensors or stereo cameras can identify smaller objects like cables, socks, or pet waste and route around them rather than getting tangled. If you have pets or children who regularly leave objects on the floor, investing in a model with robust obstacle avoidance saves a lot of retrieval frustration.
No robot vacuum handles every obstacle perfectly. Thick rugs with long pile can trip sensors. Dark-coloured mats absorb the infrared used by cliff sensors and may trigger a false floor-edge alarm. Cables left on the floor remain a common problem even on high-end models. The practical solution is a brief preparation routine before each scheduled run: pick up cables, tuck away soft toys, and clear anything fragile from floor level. This takes two minutes and dramatically improves the quality of each clean.
What to Look for When Buying a Robot Vacuum
Suction power, measured in Pascals, determines how effectively a robot picks up debris from different surface types. Hard floors don’t require enormous suction, but thick carpet — particularly high-pile or shaggy rugs — demands significantly more power to pull dirt from deep in the fibres. Most manufacturers offer adjustable suction modes; a lower setting preserves battery life on hard floors while a boost mode engages on carpet automatically when the sensor detects a change in surface texture.
Battery life and charging time determine how large an area a robot can clean in a single session. Most mid-range models handle between one hundred and two hundred square metres on a full charge, which is sufficient for most Australian homes. Larger homes, or homes with multiple levels, may need a model that supports auto-resume — the robot returns to its dock to recharge mid-clean and then picks up exactly where it stopped, rather than starting from scratch. This feature was once premium; it’s now fairly common across a wide price range.
Self-Emptying Stations: Are They Worth It?
A self-emptying dock station is the single upgrade that most meaningfully reduces the robot vacuum’s maintenance burden. Instead of opening a small dust bin after every few runs, the dock automatically suctions the contents into a sealed bag that holds several weeks’ worth of debris. For households with pets that shed heavily, or for anyone who finds the emptying process unpleasant, this feature transforms the robot from a semi-automated device into something that genuinely runs itself. The bags are consumable — typically replaced every thirty to sixty days — but the cost is modest compared to the convenience gained.
Some dock stations combine vacuuming with mopping in a single unit and include automatic mop washing and drying. These all-in-one stations represent the current high end of the category and handle a broad range of floor maintenance tasks without intervention. Whether that level of automation justifies the higher cost depends on how much floor you need to clean and how much you value completely hands-off operation. For a home with mostly hard flooring, a combined vacuum-and-mop setup from a brand like eufy can genuinely replace the need for manual mopping in normal maintenance cycles.
Setting Up Schedules and Zones for Best Results
A robot vacuum delivers the most value when it runs on a regular, automated schedule rather than only when you remember to start it. Most apps allow you to set different cleaning schedules for different days and even different rooms — a daily pass through the kitchen and entry hall, a less frequent full-house run on weekends. Once this routine is established, floors maintain a baseline cleanliness that eliminates the need for emergency cleaning sessions before guests arrive.
Room labelling and zone cleaning add another layer of control. If the kitchen has had a busy cooking session, you can send the robot to clean just that room immediately without waiting for the next scheduled run. Restricted zones — virtual walls drawn in the app — keep the robot away from pet bowls, children’s play areas, or rooms with fragile objects on the floor. Mop-free zones prevent the wet mop pad from crossing onto carpet. These controls make the robot vacuum genuinely adaptable to the way your household actually uses space, rather than forcing a one-size-fits-all cleaning pattern.
Maintenance That Keeps Performance Consistent
Robot vacuums require regular maintenance to perform well over time. The most important task is cleaning the brush rolls, which accumulate hair and fibres that wrap tightly around the mechanism and reduce suction if left unattended. Most manufacturers recommend checking brush rolls weekly and clearing them thoroughly every two to four weeks depending on use. Some models use rubber extractors instead of bristle brush rolls, which tangle significantly less and are easier to maintain — a genuine advantage in homes with long-haired pets or people.
Filters need periodic cleaning or replacement. A clogged filter forces the motor to work harder and reduces the air pressure that drives suction. Most filters can be tapped clean over a bin and rinsed occasionally, though they should be fully dry before reinsertion to avoid mould. Replacement filter packs are inexpensive and should be swapped every few months in heavy-use households. Sensors — particularly the cliff sensors on the underside and the lidar or camera on top — should be wiped gently with a dry cloth every week or two to prevent dust accumulation from affecting navigation accuracy.
Cleaner Floors, Less Time Spent Cleaning
A robot vacuum earns its place in a home not by replacing every cleaning task but by handling the high-frequency maintenance that keeps floors from becoming an ongoing source of frustration. The right model — chosen for your floor types, home size, and willingness to do minimal upkeep — runs quietly in the background, frees up genuine time, and delivers a level of floor cleanliness that manual vacuuming on a weekly schedule simply cannot match. Start by identifying the features that matter most for your specific home, compare how different navigation technologies perform in homes similar to yours, and choose a model you’ll actually trust to run on a schedule. That trust is what turns a robot vacuum from a novelty into a household essential.

articles.title: Airbound raises $37M to scale autonomous drone delivery in India
articles.text:
Airbound raises $37M to scale autonomous drone delivery in India
Bengaluru-based Airbound will use its Series A funding to expand aircraft engineering, manufacturing and commercial operations as drone delivery moves towards wider adoption in India.
Airbound, a Bengaluru-based aerospace startup developing lightweight autonomous aircraft for deliveries, has raised $37 million in a Series A round led by Greenoaks. The round also includes existing and new investors including DoorDash, Lachy Groom, Lightspeed, and Humba Ventures.
Airbound said the latest financing takes its total capital raised since its 2023 launch to nearly $50 million, including a $8.65 million seed funding round in October.
The company plans to use the money to accelerate engineering, commercial-scale manufacturing and its go-to-market efforts. That marks a shift from demonstrating the technology towards building the capacity and commercial infrastructure needed for larger-scale operations.
The startup said its aircraft have already completed more than 1,000 autonomous flights with Narayana Health, carrying diagnostic samples between healthcare facilities and cutting delivery times from hours to minutes, with no mission failures reported in those flights.
Airbound’s central argument is that conventional aircraft are inefficient for small payloads because much of their weight is devoted to carrying the aircraft itself. The company is designing an aircraft architecture that seeks to reverse that balance, so that a greater share of the weight in flight is the material being transported. Its current aircraft uses a blended wing body tailsitter design, combining the vertical take-off capability of a drone with the efficiency of a fixed-wing aircraft.
The commercial test now underway is in Andhra Pradesh. Under an agreement announced earlier this year by the company, Airbound plans to build a drone delivery network connecting three cities and eventually scale to 10,000 flights a day across retail, e-commerce and healthcare. The company believes the project is a potential model for wider aerial delivery in India.
“The bar for delivery in India is high. The benchmark is 10 minutes to your doorstep, at an extremely low cost. That’s the complexity here,” said Founder and chief executive officer Naman Pushp. “If you can build something that works in India, it tends to work anywhere.”
Pushp noted the underlying ambition is to alter the economics of moving goods, arguing that “better physics leads to better economics”. He has explained the longer-term objective even more broadly, with Airbound expecting the same technology could eventually support passenger transport. The company sees a future where a 300-kilometre journey is being completed in about 20 minutes.
The funding comes as drone logistics moves from pilot projects towards larger commercial networks. Delhi-based Skye Air Mobility raised $9 million in a Series B round in March, led by IAN Alpha Fund, to expand beyond Delhi-NCR, and to strengthen its drone operations, airspace-management and autonomous logistics systems.
Neil Shah, Partner at Greenoak said Airbound could overcome the longstanding trade-off between the speed of air freight and the low cost of road transport. “When one autonomous aircraft can move a single package with the cost efficiency of a fully loaded 20-ton truck, fast delivery and cheap delivery are no longer in tension, and roads stop being the default,” Shah added.
The regulatory environment has also been developing. India’s Drone Rules 2021 reduced several approval requirements and laid the groundwork for a more digital regulatory system, while the government said drone corridors would be developed for cargo deliveries. Last September, the government also reduced GST on drones to 5%, a move intended to support the wider drone ecosystem.
Recent activity suggests the opportunity is not limited to India. In April, FedEx and IIT Madras completed intra-city drone delivery trials in Bengaluru, using an aerial route that cut a typical road journey of about 60 minutes to roughly 21 minutes. In the US, Zipline raised more than $600 million in January to expand autonomous deliveries, while DoorDash received FAA certification in July to operate its own commercial drone service.
Edited by Megha Reddy

articles.title: Android Pulse : cette appli fantôme vient d'apparaître sur des milliers de smartphones, voici pourquoi
articles.text:
Android Pulse : cette appli fantôme vient d'apparaître sur des milliers de smartphones, voici pourquoi
Une application sans icône, au nom inconnu, s'est glissée dans les mises à jour du Play Store ce week-end. Google n'a presque rien expliqué. Voici ce qu'elle fait, et comment la retirer si vous le souhaitez.
Samedi 22 août au matin, une entrée inédite a fait son apparition dans la file des mises à jour Google Play de millions d'appareils Android : "Android Pulse". En guise d'identité visuelle, un carré blanc. En guise d'explication, une phrase absconse sur la "détection d'anomalies dans la consommation de ressources critiques". De quoi hérisser les plus aguerris.
À quoi sert Android Pulse ?
L'appli est un composant système légitime, édité par Google sous le nom de paquet com.google.android.apps.pulse. Sa vocation : surveiller en arrière-plan les dérives de consommation (batterie, processeur, mémoire vive) provoquées par le système d'exploitation ou les applications tierces.
Concrètement, Pulse distribue des règles de détection d'anomalies aux appareils Android ; quand une application s'emballe et dévore le CPU, quand un processus système vide la batterie de façon anormale, c'est ce service qui permet à Google d'identifier le problème à grande échelle. Aucune interface, aucune collecte de données personnelles documentée, aucun comportement intrusif.
Selon APKMirror, Pulse existe depuis mars 2026, totalise sept versions et dépasse les 10 millions de téléchargements. Sur les Pixel, le service était déjà préinstallé en natif, signalé par une discrète icône verte évoquant un tracé de fréquence cardiaque.
Pourquoi Android Pulse est apparu soudainement dans vos mises à jour
La perplexité collective tient à un choix de distribution aberrant. Google dispose d'un canal dédié, System Services, conçu précisément pour mettre à jour ce type de brique logicielle de manière transparente, loin des yeux de l'usager. En propulsant Pulse dans la liste des mises à jour manuelles, flanqué d'un visuel vierge et d'un descriptif calibré pour un auditoire d'ingénieurs en télémétrie, Mountain View a engendré l'exacte défiance que ce canal silencieux était censé prévenir.
Comment désinstaller ou désactiver Android Pulse
Ouvrez Paramètres > Applications > Pulse (ou Android Pulse). Le bouton "Désinstaller" sera vraisemblablement grisé, l'appli étant rattachée à la couche système. Deux options demeurent : "Désactiver" et "Forcer l'arrêt". La manipulation est rapide, son utilité, discutable. Le service ne consomme aucune ressource perceptible et alimente les mécanismes de diagnostic dont Google se sert pour améliorer la stabilité d'Android à grande échelle. Le couper revient à retirer un capteur de fumée parce qu'il ne sonne jamais.

articles.title: Massive DDoS attack disrupts Norway’s government digital services
articles.text:
A large distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attack has disrupted Norway’s shared government digital infrastructure since Monday, affecting services used by the public sector.
The attack started at 03.38 CEST on Monday and has targeted the infrastructure supporting services operated by the Norwegian Digitalization Agency, Digitaliseringsdirektoratet (Digdir), and its operations provider, Vivicta.
Digdir operates Norway’s shared digital government infrastructure, including public-service logins, electronic IDs and signatures, secure digital mail, government forms, public-record access, and data exchange between agencies.
In an announcement published earlier today, the organization states that several services were completely unavailable for short periods.
The agency says many affected systems have now been stabilized, although some services, like ID-porten and eSignering, remain partially inaccessible.
As a result of the attack, users may encounter errors such as failed connections, slow server responses, and unusually long login times.
For live updates on the availability of Digdir services, people may consult the services' operating status page as well as the incident report page with updates from Norway's Directorate for Digitization.
Digdir director Frode Danielsen says the investigation into the incident showed no indication of a security breach affecting the organization’s systems or any compromise of personal data.
Danielsen added that this is the third DDoS attack targeting Digdir recently, following one in June and another on August 3.
The Norwegian National Security Authority (NSM) and the Norwegian Data Protection Authority (Datatilsynet) have been notified accordingly.
There is currently no official attribution for the attack, although Norwegian media have speculated about potential Russian involvement.
Meanwhile, services that rely on Digdir but are not directly targeted also experience disruptions.
Altinn, Norway’s central digital platform for communication between citizens, businesses, and government agencies, published a warning about login issues and operational problems, linking to Digdir’s status page.
Skatteetaten, Norway’s tax administration agency, displays a similar notice about login issues on its website and urges users to try again later.

articles.title: Honor lance sa première montre connectée pour enfants, la Honor Kids Watch Plus
articles.text:
Avec la Kids Watch Plus, Honor propose une montre connectée entièrement conçue pour les enfants mais gérée par leurs parents. Géolocalisation, contrôle du temps d’écran et encore bouton SOS sont présents sur la première montre connectée spéciale enfant conçue par Honor.
Une montre connectée pensée pour les enfants
La Honor Kids Watch Plus est une montre connectée conçue pour les enfants, mais dont presque toutes les principales fonctionnalités sont gérées par leurs parents. En effet, pour fonctionner, la montre doit obligatoirement être synchronisée avec le smartphone d’un adulte de confiance.
Bien que ce soit une montre, la Honor Kids Watch Plus, possède un emplacement SIM qui offre la possibilité aux parents de joindre leurs enfants directement sur la montre. Les appels ne sont pas la seule fonctionnalité, la montre permet également l’envoi de SMS et d’emojis prédéfinis par les parents. Il est également possible de créer des groupes de discussions avec la famille et/ou les proches. Honor assure que la sécurité des communications est assurée par un système de filtrage, la montre se synchronise uniquement aux smartphones des adultes de confiance configurés en amont, les enfants ne peuvent alors pas être contactés par une autre personne.
Des fonctionnalités de sécurité
Honor mise sur un système fermé pour limiter les risques. La Kids Watch Plus ne dispose pas de store d’applications, ce qui empêche l’accès notamment aux réseaux sociaux et aux jeux.
La montre intègre aussi un système de géolocalisation reposant sur huit technologies. Honor indique que ce système permet de localiser l’enfant avec précision, en intérieur comme en extérieur. Les parents peuvent consulter l’historique des trajets et définir des « zones sûres ». Une notification est envoyée sur leur smartphone si l’enfant sort du périmètre défini. En cas d’urgence, un bouton SOS permet également à l’enfant de déclencher une alerte sur le téléphone des parents.
Les parents peuvent gérer le temps d’écran de leur enfant. Un mode « classe » permet quant à lui d’afficher uniquement l’heure et de bloquer les autres applications pendant les heures de cours. La montre propose également un mode sport avec différents exercices, tels que des abdominaux, des jump squats ou de la corde à sauter.
Autonomie de 5 jours, un mode sport et autres fonctionnalités
La Honor Kids Watch Plus dispose d’un bracelet en silicone et est proposée dans un seul coloris, noir. Son boîtier mesure 249 x 41,2 x 15,4 mm et la montre pèse 51 grammes avec son bracelet.
Elle embarque une batterie de 850 mAh qui devrait lui offrir jusqu’à cinq jours d’autonomie. Certifiée IP68, elle résiste aux éclaboussures et à une immersion jusqu’à 1,5 mètre pendant 30 minutes. Enfin, la Honor Kids Watch Plus embarque un capteur selfie de 2 mégapixels.
Prix et disponibilité
La Honor Kids Watch Plus est dès à présent disponible. Elle est commercialisée au prix de 99,99€ et bénéficie de deux offres de lancement en partenariat avec SFR :
- 1€ à l’achat + 3 €/mois sur 24 mois avec un forfait à 11,99 €/mois (pour les nouveaux clients SFR)
- 4,99 €/mois (si le client a déjà une box ou un smartphone chez SFR)

articles.title: Amazon will die Preise deutlich erhöhen: Bei welchen Geräten du jetzt trotzdem noch sparen kannst
articles.text:
Kindle, Echo, Fire TV: Wo du jetzt noch sparen kannst, bevor Amazon die Preise erhöht
Hinweis: Wir haben in diesem Artikel Provisions-Links verwendet und sie durch "*" gekennzeichnet. Erfolgt über diese Links eine Bestellung, erhält t3n.de eine Provision.
Amazon hat die Preise für eigene Geräte wie den E-Reader Kindle oder die smarten Echo-Lautsprecher deutlich angehoben – in vielen Fällen um 40 Prozent und mehr. In den USA erfolgte die Preissteigerung schon einige Tage zuvor. Grund dafür ist der anhaltende Speichermangel, der durch den KI-Boom verursacht wurde. Hier erfährst du, mit welchen Kosten du künftig rechnen musst und bei welchen Amazon-Produkten sich ein schneller Kauf jetzt noch lohnt.
Hersteller geben gestiegene Kosten weiter
Die aktuelle Speicherkrise hält die Elektronikbranche fest im Griff. Schuld daran ist die stark zunehmende KI-Nutzung: Um den Bedarf an Rechenleistung zu decken, entstehen derzeit viele neue Rechenzentren. Diese auszustatten, ist für Chiphersteller oft deutlich lukrativer, weshalb viele ihre Produktion umgestellt haben. In der Folge werden SSDs und Arbeitsspeicher für Computer, Laptops und Smartphones immer knapper und teurerer.
Unter den Pioneers Picks stellen wir dir regelmäßig weitere praktische Tools und Gadgets vor.
Zahlreiche Elektronikhersteller geben die gestiegenen Preise inzwischen an ihre Kund:innen weiter. Einer davon ist Apple: Wer jetzt ein neues Macbook Air kauft, zahlt rund 200 Euro mehr als noch vor wenigen Monaten. Auch das iPad kostete vor einem halben Jahr noch etwa 50 Euro weniger. Andere Hersteller wie Samsung, Dell und Lenovo haben ebenfalls schon Preiserhöhungen für ihre Produkte angekündigt.
Amazon ist damit definitiv kein Einzelfall. Viele Geräte der hauseigenen Marken sollen teurer werden, um die höheren Speicherkosten auszugleichen. Die gestiegenen Preise sind auf dem Marktplatz schon ersichtlich – allerdings sind Kindle, Echo und Co. aktuell teilweise noch deutlich reduziert. Wer jetzt bestellt, kann also sogar gegenüber dem ursprünglichen Preis ein Schnäppchen machen und die geplante Erhöhung gezielt umgehen.
Kindle Paperwhite: Jetzt noch 50 Euro sparen
Vor allem beim Kindle sind die Preise deutlich gestiegen. Das Paperwhite-Modell gehört zu den beliebtesten der E-Reader-Serie. Er zeichnet sich durch einen besonders starken Kontrast aus. Das 7-Zoll-Display ist mit der typischen E-Ink-Technologie ausgestattet, dank der es gedrucktem Papier ähnelt. Dadurch wird auch der Akku geschont: Laut Herstellerangaben hält er bis zu 128 Stunden mit einer Aufladung durch.
Das Gerät verfügt über einen internen Speicher von 16 Gigabyte und bietet damit Platz für Tausende Bücher, Zeitschriften und Comics. Kindle-Nutzer:innen kaufen E-Books direkt auf der Plattform und verwalten sie über ihr Amazon-Konto. Mit Kindle Unlimited bietet der Konzern zudem eine Art Flatrate für Vielleser:innen an. Bisher lag der Preis bei 169,99 Euro. Künftig soll der Kindle Paperwhite 209,99 Euro kosten, aktuell ist er aber noch zum alten Preis erhältlich.
Echo Dot: Smart Speaker zum Vorzugspreis
Amazons Alexa gehört zu den beliebtesten Sprachassistenten in Deutschland. Er ist über die Echo-Geräte abrufbar und kann beispielsweise Musik abspielen, einen Timer stellen oder Informationen zu Wetter und Verkehr liefern. Auch Smart-Home-Geräte wie Lampen oder Staubsaugroboter lassen sich über einen Smart Speaker steuern. Amazon bietet unterschiedliche Varianten an. Das günstigste Modell ohne Bildschirm ist der etwa handtellergroße Echo Dot.
Er lässt sich per Sprache steuern, bietet aber auch einzelne haptische Knöpfe, um die Lautstärke zu regeln oder das Mikrofon auszuschalten. Beim Neukauf ist zudem ein kostenloser Early-Access zur neuen KI-Version Alexa Plus enthalten. Bisher kostete der smarte Lautsprecher ab 64,99 Euro. Künftig soll der Einstiegspreis für alle Farbvarianten bei 89,99 Euro liegen. Aktuell ist er aber noch zum Angebotspreis von 39,99 Euro erhältlich.
Fire TV: Hier machst du noch einen guten Deal
Auch beim Fire TV Stick sollen die Preise deutlich steigen. Mit dem externen Gerät lassen sich auch ältere Fernseher internetfähig machen, um darauf Streaming-Angebote wie Netflix, Prime oder Disney Plus zu nutzen. Das macht ihn besonders bei Personen beliebt, die ihr vorhandenes Gerät nachrüsten möchten, anstatt direkt mehrere hundert Euro in ein neues Modell zu investieren.
Der Fire TV Stick HD kostete bis vor Kurzem noch 44,99 Euro. Künftig soll der Standardpreis bei 64,99 Euro liegen – ein Aufschlag von über 44 Prozent. Ähnlich sieht es beim Fire TV Stick 4K Select aus: Dieser kostete bisher 54,99 Euro, künftig liegt der Preis bei 69,99 Euro. Wer mit dem Gedanken spielt, sich einen solchen Internet-Stick zuzulegen, sollte jetzt noch schnell zuschlagen: Beide Varianten sind derzeit deutlich reduziert und schon ab 26,99 Euro erhältlich.

articles.title: Waymo annonce le lancement de ses taxis sans chauffeur dans l'Union européenne en 2027
articles.text:
On savait que Waymo avait discrètement enregistré des filiales en France, en Allemagne et en Espagne en juin 2026, on sait désormais quelle sera la première ville de l’Union européenne à découvrir les robotaxis.
Dans un billet publié le 25 août 2026, Waymo annonce préparer le lancement de son service de taxis autonomes dans la capitale bavaroise. Après Londres, prévue pour septembre 2026 mais récemment décalée, l’entreprise s’attaque pour la première fois à un pays de l’Union européenne. Si tout va bien (ce qui est peu probable), des volants tourneront seuls d’ici à la fin de l’année 2027 en Allemagne.
Des Waymo à Munich dans les prochaines semaines, mais d’abord avec un chauffeur
Le calendrier annoncé est long : Waymo est conscient des difficultés à venir en Europe. L’entreprise appliquera à Munich la méthode déjà utilisée à Londres et dans les villes américaines : dans les prochaines semaines, des véhicules Waymo circuleront dans les rues de Munich en conduite manuelle, avec un humain au volant.
Le but est de cartographier le réseau routier et d’apprendre au Waymo Driver, son modèle IA, à reproduire la conduite humaine. L’ouverture du service commercial, sans personne au volant, est visée « vers la fin 2027 », sous réserve d’obtenir des autorisations.
Le choix de Munich n’a rien d’un hasard. L’Allemagne autorise depuis 2021 l’exploitation de véhicules autonomes de niveau 4 sur la voie publique, à l’intérieur de zones d’exploitation définies. C’est le cadre juridique le plus permissif de l’Union européenne aujourd’hui, et le gouvernement allemand ne s’en cache pas.
« Le cadre juridique, nous l’avons déjà créé », se félicite Christian Hirte, secrétaire d’État parlementaire au ministère fédéral des Transports, cité par Waymo. Il ajoute que le fait qu’une entreprise comme Waymo choisisse l’Allemagne « montre l’attractivité de notre marché ». Du côté bavarois, Florian Herrmann, chef de la chancellerie d’État, promet de « réduire la bureaucratie et lever les obstacles réglementaires ». Des déclarations politiques qui ne comptent pas comme autorisations : Waymo devra négocier pendant des mois et fournir de nombreux documents pour obtenir un feu vert règlementaire.
Waymo arrivera-t-il à lancer son service sans chauffeur d’ici la fin 2027 ? La comparaison avec Tesla est éclairante sur l’état réel de la réglementation européenne. Le FSD Supervised, qui n’est qu’une aide à la conduite de niveau 2 avec un conducteur responsable en permanence, a mis des années à obtenir une première homologation de type aux Pays-Bas, en avril 2026. Elle s’est ensuite étendue à quelques pays par reconnaissance mutuelle, comme la Belgique, mais toujours pas en France ou en Allemagne. Les pouvoirs publics sont très conservateurs et exigent plus de données qu’ailleurs : Waymo, qui va plus loin que Tesla, pourrait mettre des années à obtenir le feu vert.
Le contexte a tout de même changé cet été. L’ONU a adopté en juin 2026 un premier cadre mondial pour les véhicules totalement autonomes, avec le soutien de l’Union européenne. Chaque État doit encore le transposer dans son droit national, mais l’Allemagne, en coordination avec Waymo, pourrait s’appuyer dessus pour aller plus vite.
Et la France dans tout ça ?
Pour convaincre les autorités, Waymo avance ses arguments sécurité, tous issus de ses propres données : plus de 350 millions de kilomètres parcourus en mode totalement autonome, 16 fois moins d’accidents avec blessés graves qu’un conducteur humain, 14 fois moins d’accidents avec piétons blessés et 6 fois moins avec des cyclistes. Des chiffres impressionnants qui visent à prouver que la conduite autonome est indispensable… même si les pouvoirs publics sont méfiants.
Évidemment, la question l’acceptabilité sociale se posera aussi. Munich est réputée plus calme que Paris, mais on voit déjà à Londres des chauffeurs de black cabs évoquer des tactiques de sabotage passif pour piéger les robotaxis dans la circulation. Au pays de BMW, Mercedes et Volkswagen, quelle place y aura-t-il pour les taxis autonomes de Google ?
En France, la structure Waymo France SARL existe depuis juin 2026, avec une adresse à quelques pas des Champs-Élysées. Aucune annonce n’accompagne aujourd’hui cette structure et la France ne dispose toujours pas d’un cadre commercial pour un service de niveau 4 sans conducteur. Les récentes déclarations du ministre sur Tesla FSD ne vont pas dans le sens de Waymo : il serait étonnant de découvrir Waymo à Paris dans les prochaines semaines.
Dans le meilleur des cas, des Waymo pourraient rouler dans des villes allemandes à partir de la fin de l’année 2027. Reste à savoir si Waymo débutera les tests en France, avec des chauffeurs, dans les prochains mois.
