articles.title: AMD Radeon RX 9070 vs. 9070 XT: Which Should You Buy?
articles.text:
Should you buy the Radeon RX 9070 or the RX 9070 XT? It is a question we get asked surprisingly often, so for anyone unsure which model is the better choice, we are going to cover everything, including the basics for readers who do not live and breathe this stuff.
The truth is that the RX 9070 and 9070 XT are very similar. When the cards launched, the non-XT version did not make much sense, because it cost just 8% less while packing 13% fewer cores. But it's now been over a year since these models first appeared, and pricing has fluctuated considerably. At times, the non-XT model has been significantly cheaper, which explains why so many of you have been asking about it.
In terms of specifications, both offer 16GB of 20Gbps GDDR6 memory on the same 256-bit-wide memory bus, providing 640 GB/s of bandwidth. Both also feature 64MB of Infinity Cache and support the PCI Express 5.0 x16 interface.
Where they differ is in their core configurations. The RX 9070 features 3,584 cores, whereas the XT version gets 4,096, a 14% increase. According to AMD's specifications, the RX 9070 XT also boosts to 2,970 MHz, compared with just 2,520 MHz for the non-XT model, giving it an 18% clock-speed advantage.
|  | Radeon RX 9070 XT | Radeon RX 9070 | Radeon RX 7900 XTX | Radeon RX 7900 XT | Radeon RX 7900 GRE | 
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Price (MSRP) | $600 | $550 | $1000 | $900 | $550 | 
| Release Date | Mar 2025 |  | Dec 2022 |  | Feb 2024 | 
| Process | TSMC N4P |  | TSMC N5 (GCD) / TSMC N6 (MCD) |  |  | 
| Die Size (mm2) | 357 mm2 |  | 529 mm2 |  |  | 
| Core Config | 4096 : 256 : 128 | 3584 : 224 : 128 | 6144 : 384 : 192 | 5376 : 336 : 192 | 5120 : 320 : 192 | 
| L2 Cache (MB) | 64 MB |  | 96 MB | 80 MB | 64 MB | 
| GPU Boost Clock | 2400 MHz | 2070 MHz | 2500 MHz | 2400 MHz | 2245 MHz | 
| Memory Capacity | 16 GB |  | 24 GB | 20 GB | 16 GB | 
| Memory Speed | 20 Gbps |  |  |  | 18 Gbps | 
| Memory Type | GDDR6 |  |  |  |  | 
| Bus Type / Bandwidth | 256-bit, 640 GB/s |  | 384-bit, 960 GB/s | 320-bit, 800 GB/s | 256-bit, 576 GB/s | 
| Total Board Power | 304W | 220W | 355W | 315W | 260W | 
Based on those specifications, you might expect the XT model to be considerably faster. But as is often the case, it depends.
Most models do not adhere strictly to AMD's reference clocks. The Sapphire Pure cards, for example, show only a 5 – 6% clock-speed difference between the two GPUs, while the Pulse versions are closer to 9 – 10%.
The PowerColor Hellhound RX 9070 averaged a clock frequency of 2,745 MHz, meaning the Sapphire Pure 9070 XT clocked 13% higher on average. Meanwhile, the Asus TUF Gaming RX 9070 XT averaged 3.2 GHz, putting it 17% ahead.
Given that most RX 9070 XT cards appear to have no trouble operating at around 3.2 GHz, you might assume it would be easy to overclock the non-XT models to similar frequencies. After all, they are effectively the same product, only with a few cores disabled. Unfortunately, that is not the case. Most RX 9070 cards max out at around 2.8 GHz due to power limits enforced by AMD.
The only way around this is to flash the graphics card with a different BIOS, though doing so can introduce a few complications. The BIOS requires a valid signature, meaning you need to use one from a closely related model. Ideally, that means flashing a Pure RX 9070 with a Pure RX 9070 XT BIOS, or at least using an RX 9070 XT BIOS with the same I/O configuration, including the same number of DisplayPort and HDMI outputs.
As we just noted, the RX 9070 is effectively an RX 9070 XT with some cores disabled, but those disabled cores cannot be restored. They are laser-cut at the factory, so flashing an RX 9070 XT BIOS will not re-enable them. What the new BIOS can do is significantly increase the PPT, or power limit, providing additional headroom for higher core frequencies and improved performance.
Ignoring BIOS modifications, the RX 9070 XT has 14% more cores and generally clocks around 10% higher. In our day-one review, we found that the XT was 9% faster on average at 1440p and 14% faster at 4K.
Since then, we have seen numerous display driver updates, a new Windows 11 build, game updates, and, of course, plenty of new games. While updating some of our larger GPU benchmarks, we added the RX 9070 so we could compare it with the XT version across a massive range of titles. Given how similar these products are, we will not examine all 50 graphs individually, but we will look at a few games before moving on to the average results.
Test System Specs
| CPU | AMD Ryzen 7 9800X3D | 
| Motherboard | MSI MPG X870E Carbon WiFi [BIOS 7E49v1A4] Resizable BAR Enabled | 
| Memory | G.Skill Trident Z5 RGB DDR5-6000 CL30 [CL30-38-38-96] | 
| Graphics Card | Radeon RX 9070 & 9070 XT | 
| ATX Case | MSI Prospect 700R | 
| Power Supply | Kolink Regulator Gold ATX 3.0 1200W | 
| Storage | TeamGroup T-Force Cardea A440 M.2 PCIe Gen4 NVMe SSD 4TB | 
| Operating System | Windows 11 25H2 | 
| Display Driver | AMD Radeon Adrenalin 26.7.1 WHQL | 
Benchmarks
Spider-Man 2
Starting with Spider-Man 2 using the Very High quality preset, the RX 9070 XT was 10% faster when comparing average frame rates at 1440p and 14% faster at 4K. However, the difference was more significant for the 1% lows, where the XT delivered a 21% improvement at both tested resolutions.
We saw similar margins after switching to the more demanding Ray Tracing Ultimate preset. At 1440p, the XT model was 22% faster for the 1% lows, though just 12% faster when comparing average frame rates. Moving up to 4K widened the gap considerably, with the RX 9070 XT delivering a 29% higher average frame rate and 26% stronger 1% lows. This is about the largest performance difference you can expect between these two models.
Lego Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight
Changing gears with Lego Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight, we will start with the Medium quality results. At 1440p, the RX 9070 XT was up to 10% faster, as seen in the 1% lows, with that margin increasing to 15% at 4K.
Using the more demanding Epic quality preset, the RX 9070 XT was 13% faster at 1440p and 21% faster at 4K, or 24% faster when comparing the 1% lows. Once again, it is under the most demanding test conditions that the XT model achieves its largest gains over the standard RX 9070.
007 First Light
Next up is 007 First Light, starting with the Medium quality results. At 1440p, the RX 9070 XT delivered a 12% higher average frame rate than the standard RX 9070, alongside a more modest 7% improvement in the 1% lows. Increasing the resolution to 4K widened the gap considerably, allowing the XT to pull ahead by 17% on average and 15% for the 1% lows.
Using the Ultra quality preset at 1440p, the RX 9070 XT maintained a 12% lead in average frame rates while delivering an 11% improvement in the 1% lows. At 4K Ultra, the average frame rate advantage remained at 12%, but the 1% lows improved by a more substantial 20%.
Fortnite
Looking at Fortnite in Performance Mode, the margins were remarkably slim at 1440p. The RX 9070 XT edged out the standard RX 9070 by just 3% on average and 2% for the 1% lows. Increasing the resolution to 4K widened those margins slightly to 7% for both metrics.
Stepping up to the Epic quality preset with ray tracing produced somewhat better scaling for the XT model. At 1440p, it delivered a 9% average frame rate advantage and a 10% improvement in the 1% lows. At 4K under these demanding ray tracing settings, the RX 9070 XT recorded its best result in this title, finishing 10% faster on average with 13% stronger 1% lows.
Counter-Strike 2
In Counter-Strike 2 using the Medium quality preset at 1440p, the XT model achieved a solid 14% lead in average frame rates, though that advantage shrank to 6% for the 1% lows. Moving to 4K evened things out somewhat, resulting in a 12% increase in the average frame rate and an 11% improvement in the 1% lows.
Using the Very High quality preset at 1440p, the RX 9070 XT delivered a 14% performance improvement for both the average frame rate and 1% lows. Interestingly, the gap tightened again at 4K, with the XT offering a 10% increase in the average frame rate but only a 4% uplift in the 1% lows.
Forza Horizon 6
Moving on to Forza Horizon 6, the Extreme quality preset at 1440p saw the RX 9070 XT deliver an 8% higher average frame rate alongside a 7% improvement in the 1% lows. The 4K results scaled slightly better, with the XT providing a 10% improvement across both metrics.
The real differentiation appeared after enabling the demanding Extreme + RT quality preset. At 1440p, the XT leapt ahead by 21% on average and 22% for the 1% lows. This strong scaling continued at 4K, where the RX 9070 XT finished 23% ahead for both the average frame rate and 1% lows.
Crimson Desert
Crimson Desert presented a tighter race. Using the Medium quality preset at 1440p, the RX 9070 XT was only 6% faster on average, with a minor 4% improvement in the 1% lows. At 4K, the XT stretched its legs a little more, achieving a 10% average frame rate advantage and 12% stronger 1% lows.
Switching to the Cinematic quality preset at 1440p, the XT maintained a modest 8% advantage in the average frame rate and a 6% lead in the 1% lows. Moving up to 4K resulted in a straightforward 10% improvement for both metrics over the standard RX 9070.
Arc Raiders
Finally, Arc Raiders produced some substantial gains for the XT model. At 1440p using the Epic quality preset with RT Static, the RX 9070 XT delivered a 10% higher average frame rate and a more noticeable 18% improvement in the 1% lows. At 4K using the same settings, it achieved a 12% average frame rate advantage and an 11% uplift in the 1% lows.
Maxing out the game with the Epic quality preset and RT Epic produced the largest 1% low improvements in this group of tests. At 1440p, the XT was 14% faster on average but a massive 29% faster in the 1% lows. This trend continued at 4K, where the XT delivered a 12% higher average frame rate alongside a substantial 26% improvement in 1% low performance.
Average Performance in 52 Games
Across a massive selection of games, the Radeon RX 9070 XT was 12% faster on average at both 1440p and 4K. That is broadly in line with our original review data, which placed the advantage within a 9 – 14% range based on a much smaller selection of games.
How to Undervolt Using Adrenaline
As a quick aside, these GPUs can be undervolted for better performance, and the process is both quick and easy. How far you can push the undervolt will depend on the individual GPU. We have tested numerous RX 9070 and 9070 XT graphics cards, and all of them handled a voltage offset of -80 mV. Most were stable at -100 mV, while a few managed -120 mV without issue.
To get started, open AMD Software: Adrenalin Edition and navigate to Performance > Tuning. In the GPU section, change the setting from Default to Custom, then enable the GPU Tuning, VRAM Tuning, and Power Tuning controls.
Under GPU Tuning, the only setting you need to adjust is the Voltage Offset, measured in millivolts. You want to decrease the voltage, not increase it. Reducing the voltage lowers power consumption and temperatures, giving the GPU additional headroom to maintain higher clock speeds.
The testing covered in the next section was conducted using a -100 mV offset for both the RX 9070 and 9070 XT. All of our samples remained completely stable with this setting, while some could reach -120 mV without issue.
Every model we tested also handled a VRAM frequency of 2,700 MHz, so you might as well make that adjustment before maximizing the total board power limit, which can typically be increased by 10%. As always, stability can vary between individual GPUs, so these settings should be thoroughly tested on your card.
Stock vs. Undervolted Performance
The Last of Us
With these settings applied, testing in The Last of Us Part I saw the tuned RX 9070 improve its average core clock speed by 5%, while the memory frequency increased by 7%.
The RX 9070 XT, on the other hand, recorded a smaller 3% increase in its average core clock speed, while the memory frequency again improved by 7%.
007 First Light
In 007 First Light, the tuned settings improved RX 9070 performance by up to 10%, compared with a more modest 6% increase for the RX 9070 XT. This suggests that tuning the non-XT model can help close the performance gap.
Forza Horizon 6
Forza Horizon 6 saw the RX 9070 gain 7 – 9% from the tuned settings, whereas the XT model was up to 5% faster, though we often recorded smaller improvements of just 2 – 3%.
Marvel Rivals
Finally, testing with Marvel Rivals saw the tuned settings improve RX 9070 performance by up to 12%, though gains of around 8 – 9% were more common. Meanwhile, the RX 9070 XT received a smaller 4 – 6% performance boost from the same adjustments.
Two Similar GPUs, One Simple Choice
With the Radeon RX 9070 XT offering 12% more performance on average, you generally would not want to pay much more than that for it. Keep in mind, however, that the margin can be considerably larger in certain games and under particularly demanding test conditions, sometimes reaching around 25%.
At current pricing, AMD's RX 9070 XT starts at $720, though most models cost $730 or more. Meanwhile, the standard RX 9070 starts at $630, with $650 being a more common asking price. This makes the XT model roughly 11 – 12% more expensive, putting its premium almost perfectly in line with the average performance improvement.
In other regions this will vary. In Australia, for example, the RX 9070 starts at around $900, with multiple models available at that price.
The cheapest XT model starts at $980, a mere 9% premium, though most cost around $1,000, representing an 11% premium. Based on those prices, you might as well buy the RX 9070 XT locally if you can afford the additional $100.
Ultimately, this is a case of saving around 10% in exchange for roughly 10% less performance, so neither card is clearly the wrong choice. Personally, I would choose the RX 9070 XT if the premium were 15% or less. Beyond that, the standard RX 9070 becomes the better-value option.

articles.title: Dreame’s dream of a rocket-powered car is dead
articles.text:
Dreame, the Chinese vacuum company that aspires to be a global technology giant, is reportedly shutting down its automotive project after funding from the government dried up.
Dreame’s dream of a rocket-powered car is dead
The vaporware car was obviously vaporware.
The vaporware car was obviously vaporware.
According to CarNewsChina, the company’s automotive division called “Project Starry Sky” once employed over 1,000 people, but now only a handful legal and HR staffers remain, charged with winding down the operation. In a statement, Dreame said it “recently adjusted certain operations that were in the exploratory phase,” and that going forward, it would focus on four key business areas: “smart home, outdoor/garden, smart mobility, and embodied AI.” (A spokesperson for the company didn’t respond to a request for comment.)
The news comes after China’s government issued new rules aimed at tightening oversight of the $3.4 trillion private fund industry, singling out Dreame in the process. After becoming one of the world’s largest manufacturer of vacuums, the company quickly moved into a variety of new businesses, spawning nearly a thousand affiliated ventures related to smartphones, robotics, and cars. But much of that expansion was funded by China’s government — and the government is now starting to take a closer look at how Dreame spends that money, according to CNBC.
Dreame wowed audiences at a San Francisco expo earlier this year with “Nebula Next 01 Jet Edition,” a sleek looking concept car equipped with a pair of rocket engines that theoretically can accelerate from 0 to 60 mph in 0.9 seconds. The vehicle was allegedly equipped with a sulfide-based solid-state battery with a record-breaking energy density exceeding 450 Wh/kg and a purported range of over 550 km (341.7 miles). The company claimed its boosters would deliver 100 kilo-Newtons of force.
But the concept raised a lot of questions, including some basic ones about how Dreame could make a car accelerate so quickly without breaking the laws of physics. Apparently Dreame didn’t have any answers to these questions, as the car itself was fully vaporware. Former employees told China Economy that the concept that was shown off in San Francisco lacked an actual chassis and was driven via remote control. (Concept cars are rarely “real” cars, in the technical sense — but even this is a little shocking in its level of deception.)
The news that Dreame’s vaporware car was totally vaporware will come as little shock to those familiar with the showy, boastful promises of companies that have never actually built a car suddenly deciding to build a car. Faraday Future, another Chinese companies with ambitions to build all manner of electric, autonomous vehicles, ran into this exact problem nearly a decade ago. And it also faced accusations of operating self-driving cars for public demos via offstage remote control.

articles.title: Android car systems abused by hackers to launch new malware that pulls devices into a hidden proxy network
articles.text:
Android car systems abused by hackers to launch new malware that pulls devices into a hidden proxy network
Is a botnet made out of cars called a "bot fleet"?
- Kaspersky found Android malware abusing DoFun car head units via TWCore updates
- Multi‑stage attack installs loaders and reverse proxy, aiming to build a botnet of connected cars
- Campaign attributed to MoYu Group; DoFun patched vulnerabilities after disclosure
We’ve seen botnets comprising cameras and DVRs, we’ve even seen botnets comprising smart fridges and digital frames, but we’ve never seen botnets comprising automobile infotainment systems. First time for everything.
Earlier this week, security researchers Kaspersky warned about finding a brand new Android malware targeting the car’s head unit. The victim seems to be a Chinese manufacturer called DoFun. Head units from this manufacturer, built on Android, are running an app for analytics and software updates called TWCore.
According to Kaspersky, the attackers abused TWCore’s update mechanisms, instructing it to download a malicious APK. This malware is then placed in the app’s cache directory and installed by the legitimate com.tw.core package.
No active campaigns
The researchers said this was a multi-stage attack. In the first stage, a tiny dropper with no user interface gets deployed. It decrypts embedded data, and extracts the information it needs for stage two. In the next stage, the loader contacts the attackers’ server and gets instructions about stage 3, which can be different things, from deploying additional malware, to running the “zhima” reverse proxy.
Despite its multifunctional nature, Kaspersky believes that the true goal of the campaign is to assimilate the cars into a botnet. Some cars come with a SIM slot and are connected to the internet 24/7. It is probably not an exaggeration to say that cars just might be the perfect devices for a malicious botnet.
Kaspersky attributed the campaign to MoYu Group, a threat actor known for building malicious botnets based on Android devices. In the past, this group was observed building the BadBox botnet out of Android smartphones, tablets, streaming devices, and other internet-connected hardware.
The researchers notified DoFun of their findings, and the vulnerability was quickly fixed: "We notified the vendor about the distribution scheme, and they subsequently reported fixing the security issues," the researchers said.

articles.title: Le code «123456», c'est terminé : WhatsApp change les règles de sécurité des comptes - Numerama
articles.text:
WhatsApp remet un coup de vis sur la sécurité.
La messagerie du groupe Meta a annoncé le 25 août, sur son blog officiel, une série de mises à jour destinées à renforcer la sécurité des comptes.
L’application revendique déjà plus d’un milliard d’utilisateurs ayant activé une clé d’accès (passkey), un système permettant de se reconnecter via empreinte digitale, reconnaissance faciale ou code de verrouillage d’écran, sans mot de passe classique.
La messagerie, qui compte plus de 3 milliards d’utilisateurs, veut désormais enrichir ce mécanisme de protection et propose deux autres modifications.
Ce qui change concrètement sur WhatsApp
Trois nouveautés sont donc déployées. D’abord, la gestion des clés d’accès évolue : il est désormais possible d’en enregistrer plusieurs sur un même compte, une par appareil, pour les utilisateurs jonglant entre Android et iOS. La configuration se fait toujours via Paramètres > Compte > Clés d’accès.
Ensuite, la vérification en deux étapes change de nature. Jusqu’ici limitée à un code PIN à six chiffres, cette couche de sécurité supplémentaire, censée empêcher la prise de contrôle d’un compte même en cas de vol du code de connexion à usage unique, repose désormais sur un mot de passe complet, alphanumérique et pouvant intégrer des caractères spéciaux.
L’idée est de rendre ce sésame plus difficile à deviner. WhatsApp cible d’ailleurs directement les retardataires encore sur « 123456 », les invitant à migrer sans attendre.
Une accumulation de garde-fous
Enfin, WhatsApp enrichit l’écran d’appel d’informations contextuelles, pour l’instant réservées à Android. Face à un numéro inconnu, l’utilisateur peut désormais voir si l’appel provient de l’étranger ou si des groupes WhatsApp sont partagés avec l’appelant, de quoi juger en un coup d’œil si la mise en relation a un sens.
Cette logique de mise en contexte reprend le principe déjà appliqué en août 2025 aux groupes inconnus. À l’époque, WhatsApp avait mis en place un filtre empêchant l’intégration directe d’un utilisateur ajouté par une personne hors de ses contacts. À la place, un aperçu de sécurité s’affiche en amont, nom du groupe, membres principaux, conseils de vigilance, avant de laisser le choix de rester ou de quitter.
Ces nouvelles fonctionnalités sont pour l’instant en cours de déploiement et devraient progressivement s’étendre à l’ensemble des utilisateurs.

articles.title: Netflix: Warum du künftig konkurrierende Streaming-Dienste auf der Plattform sehen könntest
articles.text:
Netflix: Warum du künftig konkurrierende Streaming-Dienste auf der Plattform sehen könntest
Wer vor dem Fernseher sitzt und ein paar entspannte Stunden mit Serien oder einem Film verbringen will, hat aktuell die Qual der Wahl. Disney Plus, Amazon Prime Video oder auch Netflix bieten zahlreiche exklusive Inhalte, was die Auswahl für so manche Streaming-User:innen erschwert und frustrierend gestaltet. Doch künftig könnte sich das zumindest bei Netflix etwas ändern.
Netflix: Kommt jetzt die Super-Streaming-App?
Wie die New York Times berichtet, soll Netflix Pläne schmieden, seine Plattform nicht mehr nur exklusiv für die eigenen Inhalte zu nutzen. Die Verantwortlichen denken darüber nach, den Streaming-Dienst auch für die Konkurrenz zu öffnen. Das geht aus den Aussagen von drei Insider:innen hervor, die mit den Plänen vertraut sind, aber anonym bleiben wollen.
Demnach gibt es derzeit Diskussionen bei Netflix, ob die Dienste von Peacock und Fox One in die Streaming-Plattform integriert werden könnten. Aktuell gäbe es laut den Insider:innen erste Gespräche, aber noch keinen Deal, den man nach außen kommunizieren könnte. Dafür gibt es auch noch zu viele ungeklärte Fragen, die Netflix-Nutzer:innen bei einer Ankündigung interessieren würden.
Die erste offensichtliche Frage wäre, wie eine solche Integration von anderen Streaming-Diensten bei Netflix aussehen würde. Entweder müsste Netflix den gesamten Katalog der Konkurrenz in die eigene Plattform aufnehmen oder ähnlich wie Amazon Prime Video über Einzelkäufe und zusätzliche Bezahlabos für Streaming-Kanäle verfügbar machen.
Erste Schritte, die Plattform zu öffnen, hat Netflix schon auf dem französischen Markt unternommen. Dort kann seit geraumer Zeit der Fernsehsender TF1 über die App des Unternehmens abgerufen werden. Denkbar wäre also, dass Netflix weitere Anbieter ins Boot holen will, um sich selbst zur Super-App für Streaming und damit zur zentralen Anlaufstelle für Filme, Serien und lokale On-Demand-Inhalte zu machen.

articles.title: How Tejaswini's MurariJyoti Welfare Foundation is transforming women's lives in Bihar
articles.text:
How Tejaswini's MurariJyoti Welfare Foundation is transforming women's lives in Bihar
Tejaswini returned from London to Bihar and started talking to women about menstrual health. That conversation grew into the MurariJyoti Welfare Foundation, which has now reached 3,500 people across menstruation, diabetes, hypertension and cervical cancer awareness.
While talking to women in a small community in Bihar, Tejaswini had never imagined that these very conversations would one day shape the direction of an entire organisation. It began with menstruation. Then the women spoke about their other problems. ASHA workers explained what the villages needed. The questions kept growing, and with them, so did the scope of the work.
Today, the MurariJyoti Welfare Foundation (MJWF) has reached around 3,500 people. The organisation is working with about 1,500 women and has distributed more than 500 menstrual cups. But the notable part of this journey is not the numbers. What stands out is that this work did not begin with a big project or with funding. It began with a conversation.
Efforts like these carry their own significance in understanding women's health needs in Bihar. Alongside the work being done by the Bihar government on health and awareness, women like Tejaswini, working at the grassroots, are also carrying this effort at change forward.
In this context, YourStory recently spoke with Tejaswini, founder of the MurariJyoti Welfare Foundation (MJWF). She explained how important it is to speak directly with women in villages and small communities, to understand their health needs and to give them the right information.
One question that changed a life
Tejaswini's social work was not a decision taken on any single day. It began in her childhood.
Her childhood was spent in boarding schools in Bihar and Darjeeling. Her family gave her the freedom to make her own choices and to ask questions. Understanding the body and the mind, meditation, sport and studies were all part of how she was raised.
At around the age of 12 or 13, an incident changed the way she thought. The daughter of a woman who worked in their home came asking for help, distressed by domestic violence. Tejaswini told her mother that the girl should be allowed to stay with them.
Her mother asked her a question: if she wanted to change someone's life, how much power did she have to do it?
At the time, Tejaswini could not fully grasp the question. But as she grew older, its meaning became clearer.
Tejaswini says, "Empathy alone is not enough to empower someone. You also need knowledge, understanding, resources and capability. If you stand with someone, you have to be capable enough to bring real change into their life when the need arises."
Studied psychology in London
Tejaswini studied Mass Media. During the lockdown, when she spent close to a year with her family, she saw several mental health problems around her. She felt that people were struggling, but were unable to talk about what they were going through.
This is where the desire to study Psychology seriously came from. She completed an MSc in Psychology from the University of Essex.
After that, in London, she worked on cases relating to violence against women. As an Independent Domestic Violence Advocate, she worked with women going through domestic violence and other complex situations.
During this period she also had to work with doctors, the police, schools, health services and people connected with immigration.
This experience helped her understand that a woman's safety and her health cannot be viewed separately.
Tejaswini explains, "The circumstances of the women there were different, but many of the questions were the same. How safe is a woman, how well does she understand her own body, and how far can she make her own life decisions."
Back in Bihar, it began with one cup
After returning to Bihar in 2023, Tejaswini met Sajni, a woman who worked in her home. The conversation turned to menstruation. It was during this that the menstrual cup came up.
Sajni was hearing about it for the first time. Later, she asked for a menstrual cup for her daughter as well.
For Tejaswini this was a small but significant experience. She realised that information which was ordinary for her could be entirely new for another woman.
After this she began talking to ASHA workers. Then came a pilot research study. Slowly, the foundation of MJWF's work took shape.
In the beginning, Tejaswini continued working in London. She covered the organisation's costs from her own earnings. Her thinking was that it was first necessary to understand what the community actually needed.
In March 2026 she returned to India and joined MJWF full time. In July 2026 the organisation also received Goonj's Grassroots Award.
Today, MJWF's partners include the University of Essex and the UK health innovation company 10zyme, as well as Bhagalpur Medical College and the Bihpur Primary Health Centre.
The need showed the way
MJWF's work did not stop at menstruation. ASHA workers pointed to the need for conversations with girls in schools. After this, there was an effort to help boys understand menstruation and women's health too.
Then the community saw some other problems. People reported complaints of diabetes, hypertension and cervical cancer.
After this, NCD health camps began. People were screened free of cost. They were given information about the free medicines and services available at government hospitals.
Tejaswini says the expansion of MJWF's work did not happen according to any fixed plan. She goes on to explain, "One need led to another need. The community told us that diabetes and hypertension were big problems too. Then the health camps began. We also learned that many people did not even know about the facility of free medicines at government hospitals."
Trust matters most
While working in rural areas, the biggest challenge was not resources. It was trust.
In the beginning, people would ask why someone from outside was coming among them. Talking about subjects like women's health and the body was not easy.
The team did not rush. It kept going back into the community again and again. After several months, people began to recognise them. Conversations became easier and trust grew stronger.
The situation is now changing. In many places, people have begun asking about their next need themselves.
According to Tejaswini, this is the crucial milestone for any social organisation: when a community begins raising its own questions instead of waiting for an outsider to arrive.
Now the focus is on education, employment and entrepreneurship
Alongside health, MJWF is now also considering opportunities in education, employment and entrepreneurship for women.
But Tejaswini does not want to impose any fixed model on the community. Her approach is to understand the problem first. Then research. After that, the solution.
Tejaswini says, "I do not want to decide what a community's future should look like. My effort is that people should be listened to first, then research should be done to understand the problem, and only after that should we build what is genuinely needed."
This is the aspect that makes MJWF's story a little different from other social organisations. It did not begin with a grand roadmap. There was no ready-made model. There was a conversation, there were some questions, and there was a willingness to listen to them.
Today the scope of those questions has widened. From menstruation to NCDs. From health to education and employment.
But the core idea remains the same. Listen first. Then understand. After that, act.
For Tejaswini, success will perhaps not come on the day MJWF reaches the largest number of people. The more important day will be when the community begins to recognise its own needs and is in a position to make its own decisions.
In closing, Tejaswini says, "If one day they no longer need us, that will perhaps be the greatest success of our work."
Perhaps for a social organisation there could be no better destination than that.

articles.title: Microsoft PowerToys adds Alt+Tab-style switching for an app's windows
articles.text:
Microsoft updated its Windows PowerToys toolset with a new utility dubbed "Window Hopper" that lets users switch between an app's windows more quickly.
The Window Hopper added in this release works like the standard ALT + TAB Windows feature, but it only works for the currently focused app, helping users switch back and forth between its windows.
"Once the utility is enabled, press the configurable Alt + backtick shortcut to cycle through that app's windows without stepping through everything else on your desktop," Microsoft explains.
"It is especially useful when you're juggling multiple browser windows, terminals, File Explorer windows, or editor instances."
Those who want to customize the default activation keyboard shortcut can also do so in PowerToys settings to switch to the next and previous app window.
The new feature is included in PowerToys version 0.101.2362.0, released today, along with a new compact mode for the Command Palette quick launcher that opens the tool as a search box at a configurable vertical position.
This version also adds support for PowerDisplay linked controls to adjust brightness across all displays at the same time and Windows-key activation for Shortcut Guide, a PowerToys tool introduced in June that displays keyboard shortcuts for Windows and the current active app.
Additional improvements include DemoMirror, a new ZoomIt feature that allows you to mirror a region of the screen, a window, or the entire screen onto a second monitor, and a new Mouse Highlighter ripple mode for composition-based effects on mouse clicks.
In January, Microsoft released PowerToys 0.97, which added CursorWrap, a new mouse utility for multi-monitor setups that "teleports" the mouse pointer to the opposite edge of active monitors and makes it easier to drag cursors across large screen distances.
PowerToys is now available through the official GitHub repository, which also provides a detailed changelog for each version.
Microsoft PowerToys was released during the Windows 95 era and started as a collection of small freeware tools created by Windows developers as personal projects.
However, in 2019, Microsoft revived the project as an open-source utility pack designed to enhance Windows functionality and streamline tasks previously requiring third-party tools.

articles.title: ChatGPT Plus : pourquoi OpenAI remet brutalement des limites d'utilisation
articles.text:
Mauvaise nouvelle pour les habitués de ChatGPT, la période de liberté totale n’aura été que de courte durée. Après quelques semaines pendant lesquelles un plafond hebdomadaire était appliqué, OpenAI fait machine arrière. Thibault Sottiaux, responsable ingénierie pour Codex et ChatGPT, a officialisé ce retour en arrière qui touche de nouveau les abonnés à ChatGPT Plus, qui payent 23 € par mois.
OpenAI veut préserver ses serveurs
Cette nouvelle règle s’applique dès le 25 août sur ChatGPT Work et Codex. La suppression temporaire du plafond de cinq heures avait suivi le lancement de GPT-5.6, mais l’entreprise préfère aujourd’hui réintroduire ce mécanisme pour lisser la charge sur ses capacités de calcul. L’objectif affiché est de conserver des quotas hebdomadaires généreux sans pour autant asphyxier les ressources.
 Tomorrow we will bring back the 5h limit for Plus accounts across ChatGPT Work and Codex. I had mentioned this a while ago, but then postponed it.
This is necessary as (a) the 5h limit allows us to smoothen the load on our compute, allowing to keep the plan generous in terms of…
— Tibo (@thsottiaux) August 25, 2026
Selon les explications du responsable, la formule Plus cible des profils plutôt occasionnels ou des nouveaux venus. En brûlant l’intégralité de leur crédit hebdomadaire d’un coup sans s’en rendre compte, ces utilisateurs se retrouvaient souvent bloqués. Le découpage par fenêtres de cinq heures entend ainsi forcer une meilleure répartition de l’usage sur plusieurs jours.
Les abonnés à ChatGPT Pro épargnés pour le moment
Une fois le plafond de cinq heures ou le quota de la semaine atteint, l’accès est bloqué dans l’attente d’une réinitialisation du cycle. Les utilisateurs ont alors la possibilité d’acheter des crédits supplémentaires, même si OpenAI distribue occasionnellement des réinitialisations gratuites ou permet d’en cumuler via des parrainages et des promotions.
Ce bridage ne concerne pour l’instant pas les abonnés Pro, qui ne restent soumis qu’à la limite hebdomadaire globale. Cette exception pourrait toutefois ne pas durer puisque OpenAI prévient que ce plafond de cinq heures risque d’être aussi activé sur les comptes Pro d’ici deux mois. De leur côté, les offres Enterprise et Edu continuent d’utiliser leur système de crédits, sans subir cette modification.

articles.title: What Is an Antidetect Browser? A Complete Guide for 2026 - Tech Guide
articles.text:
What Is an Antidetect Browser? A Complete Guide for 2026
Every time you open a website, that website knows more about you than you probably realise.
Not just your IP address – although that’s one of them. Websites can track the exact version of your web browser, the fonts you have on your computer, the resolution of your screen, the hardware configuration of your graphics card, your time zone, your language preferences, the way your browser handles certain renderings, and numerous other technical details which combine to create something known as a browser fingerprint.
That fingerprint is unique. Or close enough to unique that platforms can use it to identify you across sessions, link multiple accounts back to a single user, and apply restrictions accordingly.
An antidetect browser is the tool that changes this equation — by replacing your real browser fingerprint with a controlled, credible alternative that makes each browsing session appear to originate from a different device, a different user, a different context entirely.
Understanding Browser Fingerprinting
In order to comprehend the role of anti-detect browsers and their purpose, you will have to comprehend what browser fingerprinting means and how extensively modern platforms utilize it.
When you access a certain site, your browser automatically transfers a large volume of technical information along with the normal process of web communication. These platforms collect this information and create a profile of your device and web environment.
The parameters that make up a browser fingerprint include:
User Agent String – What web browser and version you are using, in what operating system, on what kind of device.
Screen properties — resolution, colour depth, pixel ratio and how your device handles high-density displays.
WebGL and Canvas fingerprints — the way your graphics processing unit renders specific graphical tasks produces a pattern that is highly specific to your hardware and driver combination.
Installed fonts and plugins — the fonts available on your operating system and any browser extensions or plugins you have installed both contribute to the fingerprint profile.
JavaScript and CSS behaviour — how your browser handles specific scripting and styling tasks reveals information about the browser engine, its version and its configuration.
Audio fingerprinting — the way your device processes audio through the browser API produces a measurable signature.
Timezone, language and locale settings — these reveal your geographic context and are cross-referenced against your IP address to identify inconsistencies.
Individually, any of these parameters is unremarkable. Collectively, the combination creates an identifier that is often more reliable for tracking and identification than a cookie — because cookies can be deleted, while your hardware and software configuration cannot be changed on a session-by-session basis without specific tools.
What an Antidetect Browser Actually Does
A standard browser — Chrome, Firefox, Safari — presents your real fingerprint to every website you visit. The antidetect browser is able to create and control several isolated browser profiles, which show various and authentic fingerprints when they visit websites.
The keyword is credible. Simply randomising fingerprint parameters produces a profile that anti-fraud systems identify as anomalous — the combination of parameters does not correspond to any real device configuration. A high-quality antidetect browser generates fingerprints based on real device profiles, producing combinations of parameters that exist in the wild and would not be flagged as suspicious by the detection systems that major platforms employ.
Each profile in an antidetect browser operates in complete isolation. Cookies, local storage, cache, and session data do not cross between profiles. When a profile is opened on a given platform, that platform sees only the data associated with that specific profile — it has no visibility into the existence of other profiles on the same device.
Combined with proxy services that assign each profile a distinct IP address, this isolation allows a user to operate multiple accounts on the same platform from a single device, with each account appearing to the platform as a genuinely separate user on a separate device in a separate location.
Who Uses Antidetect Browsers and Why
The group of users for antidetect browsers includes various types of professionals who really require multiple accounts and/or browsing privacy.
The case with affiliate marketers and media buyers is that they always have to manage several advertising accounts on different platforms such as Facebook, Google Ads, and TikTok. However, due to some rules of each platform, one is allowed to use only a few accounts at a time; therefore, all the accounts linked with the same fingerprint or IP are usually banned simultaneously.
E-commerce operators running multiple storefronts across platforms like Amazon, eBay, and Shopify face similar multi-account requirements. Managing separate seller accounts for different product categories or markets requires isolation between accounts that a standard browser cannot provide.
Web scraping and data collection professionals use antidetect browsers to gather publicly available information at scale without triggering the rate-limiting and blocking mechanisms that platforms apply to repetitive automated requests from identifiable sources.
Crypto and Web3 participants managing multiple wallets, participating in token launches or managing bounty and airdrop campaigns across platforms like CoinList need genuine account separation to operate effectively.
Digital agencies managing advertising, social media and marketing accounts on behalf of multiple clients need reliable account isolation to prevent platforms from linking client accounts together.
Privacy-conscious individuals use antidetect browsers to limit the behavioural profiling that advertising networks build through fingerprint tracking across websites — maintaining more genuine anonymity than private browsing modes or standard VPNs provide.
How Antidetect Browsers Differ From Regular Privacy Tools
The thing that must be clarified regarding an antidetect browser is that there are other tools available which address online privacy-related problems but are often mistaken for having antidetect features.
Incognito/Private Browsing prevents your browser from saving your local history, cookies, and form data. However, this will not change your browser’s fingerprint. There’s no way you can bypass the detection of a platform if it spots multiple accounts with the same fingerprints at different IP addresses.
Cookie managers and blockers prevent tracking through cookies and similar mechanisms. They do not address fingerprint-based identification, which operates independently of cookie state.
An antidetect browser addresses the fingerprint layer specifically — the deep technical parameters that persist regardless of IP address or cookie state. When combined with proxy services, it provides genuinely comprehensive account isolation rather than partial privacy that sophisticated detection systems can see through.
What to Look For in an Antidetect Browser
The quality of fingerprint generation is the most important factor in evaluating any antidetect browser. Fingerprints that do not correspond to real device configurations are detectable — the whole point of the exercise is to produce profiles that look like genuine users, which requires a constantly updated database of real device parameters and careful attention to consistency between the various parameters that make up a complete fingerprint.
Kernel update frequency matters significantly. Antidetect browsers built on a Chromium base need to track Chrome version updates closely, because a browser reporting an outdated Chrome version alongside other parameters from a current configuration creates a detectable inconsistency. Providers that update their kernel quickly maintain the credibility of their fingerprints as Chrome releases new versions.
Profile isolation architecture determines how completely separate profiles actually are. Profiles should share no storage, no cache, no process state — any leakage between profiles undermines the isolation that makes the tool useful.
Team management features matter for professional use cases where multiple people need to access and manage profile portfolios. Role-based access control, action logging and profile sharing capabilities determine whether an antidetect browser can support team-based workflows efficiently.
Proxy integration — built-in proxy management or clean integration with external proxy providers — affects how easily the fingerprint isolation provided by the browser combines with IP-level separation to produce genuinely complete account isolation.
Frequently Asked Questions
Q: Is using an antidetect browser legal?
 Using an antidetect browser is legal in most jurisdictions. The tool itself is a browser that manages fingerprint parameters — it does not interact with platforms in ways that are inherently illegal. Whether specific use cases comply with platform terms of service is a separate question that depends on how the tool is used and which platforms are involved.
Q: Can platforms detect that you are using an antidetect browser?
Antidetect browsers that offer high quality based on true device fingerprints and up-to-date browser engines are made to imitate legitimate Chrome sessions. The effectiveness of this depends on the quality of fingerprint generation, the currency of the kernel version and the consistency of all fingerprint parameters — which is why the technical quality of the provider matters significantly.
Q: Do you need a proxy to use an antidetect browser effectively?
 For multi-accounting purposes, yes. An antidetect browser manages the fingerprint layer, but if multiple profiles share the same IP address, that shared address can still link accounts together. Combining antidetect fingerprint management with separate IP addresses per profile provides the most complete account isolation.
Q: What is the difference between profiles in an antidetect browser?
 Each profile is a completely isolated browsing environment with its own fingerprint parameters, cookies, local storage, cache, and session data. From the perspective of any website visited through a given profile, that profile appears as a distinct user on a distinct device — with no visible connection to other profiles operated through the same antidetect browser installation.
The Bottom Line
Browser fingerprinting has made simple multi-account management and genuine browsing privacy significantly harder to achieve through conventional tools. VPNs change IP addresses. Incognito mode clears cookies. Neither addresses the fingerprint layer that modern platform detection systems rely on most heavily.
An antidetect browser addresses this layer specifically — creating and managing isolated profiles with credible, real-device-based fingerprints that allow professionals to operate multiple accounts with genuine separation, or individuals to browse without contributing to the behavioural profiles that advertising networks build through fingerprint tracking.

articles.title: Mac mini M6 vs Mac mini M4 : ce qui change entre les deux générations
articles.text:
Le Mac mini M4 avait déjà marqué les esprits, avec un boîtier de moins de treize centimètres de côté et un tarif d’entrée très attractif. Le nouveau modèle Mac Mini 2026 reprend ce format ultra compact et cette approche : Apple ne s’est pas attaqué au châssis et a surtout concentré ses efforts sur le processeur, la partie graphique et l’intelligence artificielle, notamment avec la toute nouvelle puce M6 fraîchement présentée par la marque à la pomme.
    À lire aussi : 
    Apple annonce son nouveau Mac Mini M6 : plus puissant, plus cher
Alors, en quoi le Mac mini M6 se démarque du Mac mini M4 ? Réponse (théorique) dans ce comparatif.
Tableau comparatif
| Caractéristiques | Mac mini M4 (2024) | Mac mini M6 (2026) | 
|---|---|---|
| Gravure | 3 nm (2ᵉ génération) | 2 nm | 
| CPU | 10 cœurs (4 + 6) | 12 cœurs (2 + 4 + 6) | 
| GPU | 10 cœurs | 12 cœurs, accélérateur neuronal par cœur | 
| Neural Engine | 16 cœurs | Double moteur, 16 cœurs | 
| Bande passante mémoire | 120 Go/s | 170 Go/s | 
| Mémoire unifiée | 16 à 32 Go | 16 à 32 Go | 
| Sans-fil | Wi-Fi 6E, Bluetooth 5.3 | Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6 | 
| Ethernet | Gigabit (option 10 Gb) | 2,5 Gb (option 10 Gb) | 
| Thunderbolt | 3 × Thunderbolt 4 | 3 × Thunderbolt 4 | 
| Prix de lancement (US) | 599 $ | 899 $ | 
La puce : le passage au 2 nanomètres
La principale différence repose sur la finesse de gravure de la puce. Le M4 s’appuyait sur un procédé 3 nanomètres de deuxième génération, quand le M6 inaugure ici le 2 nanomètres chez Apple.
Ce progrès permet de loger davantage de transistors sur une surface équivalente, ce qui se traduit par un gain à la fois en performances et en consommation. C’est sur cette base qu’Apple a revu chacun des blocs de la puce.
Processeur : douze cœurs et une nouvelle organisation
Le processeur passe de dix à douze cœurs. Le M4 s’appuyait sur quatre cœurs de performance et six cœurs d’efficacité, quand le M6 réorganise l’ensemble autour de deux « super cœurs » chargés des tâches les plus lourdes en usage isolé, de quatre cœurs hautes performances et de six cœurs basse consommation pour les traitements de fond. Apple annonce des performances processeur supérieures d’environ 40 % à celles du Mac mini M4.
Partie graphique et jeu
Le processeur graphique suit la même logique, avec douze cœurs sur le Mac mini M6 contre dix sur le M4. La nouveauté la plus concrète est l’accélérateur neuronal présent dans chaque cœur graphique, une première sur le Mac mini. Apple évoque jusqu’à deux fois plus d’images par seconde avec le ray tracing sur un titre comme Cyberpunk 2077 : Ultimate Edition, par rapport au M4.
Le M6 embarque aussi une architecture de shaders remaniée et une mise en cache dynamique revue, là où le M4 disposait déjà du ray tracing accéléré mais sans ces optimisations.
Intelligence artificielle : le vrai axe de la mise à jour
Le Mac mini M4 disposait d’un Neural Engine à seize cœurs ; le M6 en embarque deux, réunis dans un « double moteur neuronal » de seize cœurs qu’Apple annonce jusqu’à deux fois plus rapide que la génération précédente. Les frameworks système peuvent solliciter les deux moteurs en même temps, ce qui accélère l’exécution des modèles.
Combiné aux accélérateurs neuronaux du GPU, ce dispositif permet à la marque d’avancer des performances d’IA jusqu’à quatre fois supérieures à celles du Mac mini M4. Sur le traitement de requêtes vers un grand modèle de langage dans LM Studio, Apple estime que son Mac mini M6 est 4,8 fois plus rapide pour traiter les demandes, par rapport au M4.
Mémoire et stockage
La capacité mémoire ne bouge pas sur le papier : 16 Go de mémoire unifiée en entrée, jusqu’à 32 Go en option, comme sur le M4. La bande passante progresse en revanche, de 120 à 170 Go/s, ce qui aide lors du multitâche et de l’exécution de modèles en local. Côté stockage, Apple annonce un débit deux fois plus rapide, sans revoir les capacités communiquées à ce stade.
Connectivité : le rattrapage sur le sans-fil
Les ports ne changent pas d’une génération à l’autre : deux ports USB-C et une prise casque en façade, trois ports Thunderbolt 4, un port HDMI et l’Ethernet à l’arrière. L’évolution se situe sur le sans-fil et le réseau. Le Mac mini M6 passe au Wi-Fi 7 et au Bluetooth 6, contre du Wi-Fi 6E et du Bluetooth 5.3 sur le M4, et l’Ethernet intégré monte à 2,5 Gbit/s, l’option 10 Gbit/s restant disponible en configuration.
Le M6 ajoute par ailleurs la prise en charge du genlock en USB-C, pour synchroniser précisément un écran et une caméra.
Prix et disponibilité
Le Mac mini M6 est proposé à partir de 899 dollars aux États-Unis, en précommande depuis le 25 août pour une disponibilité au 22 septembre. Apple n’a pas communiqué de tarif en euros dans son communiqué, mais l’écart avec la génération précédente est tout de même flagrant : le Mac mini M4 avait débuté à 599 dollars outre-Atlantique, et à 699 euros en France.
Précisons tout de même que Mac mini M4 n’est plus vendu 599 dollars : son tarif d’entrée est en effet passé à 799 dollars fin juin 2026, à la faveur d’une hausse qu’Apple avait justifiée par le coût de la mémoire. L’écart réel au lancement du M6 est donc de 100 dollars.
Faut-il passer du M4 au M6 ?
Sur les usages courants, de la bureautique à la navigation en passant par la photo et un peu de montage, le Mac mini M4 reste une très bonne machine. La bascule vers le Mac mini M6 ne se justifie potentiellement pas pour toute personne ayant récemment acheté un M4.
L’intérêt du nouveau modèle se concentre surtout sur le calcul lié à l’intelligence artificielle : exécution de grands modèles de langage en local, mise à l’échelle d’images, tâches d’agents. Ceux qui travaillent régulièrement avec ces outils tireront parti du double moteur neuronal et des accélérateurs intégrés au GPU.

articles.title: Google's TPUv8s for Training and Inference at Hot Chips 2026
articles.text:
Google’s rate of development for their tensor processor units (TPUs) has been nothing short of remarkable. The company is already preparing their eighth generation of TPUs, which were announced a bit earlier this year.
The TPUv8 family includes both the TPU 8t for training, as well as the TPU 8i for inference, making Google’s hardware offerings unique among the hyperscalers. Whereas the other operators have been focused solely on developing inference hardware while relying on commodity hardware for training, Google has continued to develop their own hardware for both tasks right up to the current day. This experience, Google has argued in the past, is part of what has given them an edge in this market. And the TPUv8 family is meant to extend that.
Google’s TPUv8s for Training and Inference at Hot Chips 2026
Besides providing their own internal chip design for inference, the TPU 8i is also notable for being a major consumer of Google’s in-house developed CPU, the Axion. TPU 8i chips are paired with Axion CPUs in a 2-to-1 ratio inside Google’s nodes. Previously, the company was using x86 CPUs for this task, so the switch to Axion has both moved Google to their own hardware and has moved them over to the Arm architecture in the process.
Briefly, here is a quick look at the history of Google’s TPU development, which is now on their eighth generation. The first TPU was a PCIe card optimized for inference. The next TPU was a design optimized for training with shared memory. The company has (roughly) alternated between inference-optimized chips and training-optimized chips. This has fed into each other, as roughly one-third of the forward pass on training is also a type of inference.
Over the years, Google has been able to increase performance by a million-fold.
At this point Google is also designing these chips to build for the world. Rather than just building for their internal workloads, there is a bit more consideration for cloud customer workloads (though Google’s internal workloads are still very important to them).
What’s new in the eighth-gen TPUs? This year, they are doing two chips in a single year rather than alternating. Due to the wider range of applications, they are seeing a greater need for separate chips. MoE in particular imposes new bottlenecks, as it involves a lot more in the way of communication/network traffic than earlier models. Scaling up FLOPS is not enough.
This generation of hardware is also better optimized to handle the long context windows of agentic AI.
Now for a brief audience participation pop quiz. Looking at two chips (without their names), how can you tell which is which? The chip on the left is smaller with 6 HBM stacks, the one on the right is larger with 8 HBM stacks. A few people think the one on the left is the inference chip. Most people think the one on the right is the inference chip.
The answer is that the left chip is for training (8t) and the one on the right is for inference (8i).
(Someone has just made the point that everyone has the slides in advance)
But the point is that inference needs more HBM per unit of compute. Inference also needs a higher percentage of SRAM to compute.
Looking at the cost of inference, the price goes up quickly the lower the latency is. This is the classic point of inference throughput dropping with higher per-user rates.
For their own chip, Google has invested in more SRAM, more memory, and more bandwidth for the 8i.
The 8i supports multiple topologies. One particular example here is the BoardFly Topology, with is 8 trays of 4 TPUs, with 36 groups in total.
Previously, Google has used a 3D Torus. This is more optimal for training than it is for inference. Fly networks in general have lower latency, which is important for inference. The BoardFly network for 8i has a maximum of 7 hops, versus 16 hops for the torus.
The TPU8i design is optimized to perform in-network collectives efficiently. This processing is handled in the ICI I/O die near the edge of the chip next to the networking hardware, rather than processing it in the compute die. This saves the time to transfer to the compute die (including the time to physically move the data) as well as eliminating the HBM accesses.
At a high level, the 8i is similar to previous TPU inference designs. Each enclosed box is a compute die, while the purple box is the I/O die.
Now shifting gears to the training side of TPUv8 with the TPU 8t chip.
No one wants to build an optimized training solution. Training is hard, and Google wants to take it on. Google has been very successful in this regard, with existing products like Ironwood in use today with customers. Google doesn’t like to make compromises here, hence the separate training and inference chips. Dark silicon eats up precious area and parts of the power budget.
Training requires lot of FLOPS, and lots of connectivity. Which is where the focus has been in the design of the chip.
Looking at the big picture, the 8t superpod will have 9600 chips, with access to an aggregate 2PB of shared HBM memory. In terms of compute, this is 121 EFLOPS of FP4 compute. In terms of energy efficiency, this is around twice the perf-per-watt as the TPUv7 Ironwood.
Not all functions map to FP4, however. So while FP4 is very useful to have, the chip needs to efficiently handled mix precision training recopies, which is how Google has been able to reach that 2x perf-per-watt figure.
Here’s a look at a 9600 chip scale-up domain via the use of Google’s optical circuit switch (OCS). It provides both redundancy and reliability. OCS can dynamically configure slices from within the larger pod. Any slice size or shape can be created.
OCS also handles bad chips, dropping chips when they go bad, allocating a spare node, restoring from a checkpoint, and then moving on.
In previous generation TPUs, Google used their overall data center network. That changes in 8t, where they introduce the dedicated Virgo network architecture. This supports 134K TPUs in a single domain, for 47 Pbits/second of bandwidth.
Virgo uses a two layer switching topology.
As always, RAS is a huge priority for Google. The working assumption is that the chips will be flaky, so the architecture needs to be able to account for this and work around failed chips. One new RAS feature on this generation is in-field unit testing, which runs during idle cycles to test chips to see if any part of them has failed.
Failure rates also increase exponentially with temperatures, which means cooling is critical for Google. The Arrhenius equation says that chemical degradation (and semicon wear) roughly doubles for every 10-15C increase in operating temperature.
Here is the block diagram of the 8t, which is very similar to past designs. Only a few training-specific features have been changed.
And a look at a complete TPU 8t tray, with 4 TPUs per tray. This is the first time that Google is liquid cooling their optics as well. Previously those were air-cooled.
Building up from that, we have the 8t rack. There are 300 of them in Google’s superpod.
Google is also using AI to help design their TPUs. These AI models have been able to trim the power usage of TPU 8t, as well as saving area on various bits of both the training and inference chips, allowing Google to pack in more computational cores overall.
And briefly on the software front, existing codebases are fully compatible with the TPUv8 generation. Though using Google’s custom kernel language, Pallas, allows writing hardware-aware kernels directly in Python will deliver the best possible performance on both 8t and 8i.
Google has been building training and inference chips over the last decade. They are accelerating it this time by doing both together. But their larger design philosophy has not changed, employing a strong co-design link between their software (compiler) and hardware developers in order to avoid doing any more than they have to at runtime.

articles.title: 👨🏿🚀TechCabal Daily – New landlord, same old tenant | TechCabal
articles.text:
Happy Eid ul-Mawlid. ☪️
It’s a packed newsletter today. Let’s get into it.
Become smarter about tech and commerce in Francophone Africa, and the policies shaping them. Read previous editions here first and subscribe below.
M&A
MTN secures Nigeria’s approval to acquire IHS Towers
MTN Group, Africa’s largest telecom company, has cleared a major hurdle in its $2.2 billion takeover of IHS Towers in Nigeria. But regulators have ensured the telecom giant doesn’t get the whole tower cake.
What happened? Nigeria’s Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Commission (FCCPC), the competition watchdog, has given MTN conditional approval to acquire the remaining stake in IHS, with one important catch: MTN must sell up to 30% of its stake in IHS Nigeria to local investors at market prices over time.
Between the lines: The condition is aimed at preventing MTN from having too much control over the infrastructure its competitors depend on. IHS Nigeria operates nearly 16,000 towers used by MTN Nigeria, Airtel, and T2 Mobile (formerly 9mobile). In other words, MTN is buying the landlord while remaining one of the biggest tenants.
Explain like I’m new here: In February, MTN agreed to buy the remaining 19.2% of IHS Towers Nigeria for about $2.2 billion, after already holding a stake in the tower company. The deal would make MTN the majority owner of one of Africa’s biggest tower operators, giving it more control over infrastructure used by rival telcos
State of play: MTN will retain majority ownership, giving it greater control over network expansion, costs and capacity while still allowing competitors access to the towers. The deal could also help MTN recover some of the capital tied up in the acquisition and reduce pressure on its balance sheet.
The bigger issue is whether infrastructure ownership can deliver efficiency without weakening competition. Towers are becoming increasingly important as operators expand mobile broadband and 5G networks, making control of them strategically valuable.
Zoom out. For MTN, the FCCPC approval means the IHS deal is moving closer to completion. But in Nigeria’s telecom market, owning the towers comes with a reminder from regulators: you can be the landlord, just don’t change the rent because you own the building.
Every business owner needs to watch this.
The business questions you Google, answered by experts. Watch for free.
Companies
MTN is building a home for Africa’s AI ambitions
MTN wants to do more than connect Africa’s businesses to the internet; it wants to build and operate the facilities that store and process the cloud software, enterprise tools, and artificial intelligence applications those businesses use. The South African telecoms company has created Africa Data Hub Holding Limited, a new company that will develop data centre capacity across Africa backed by an undisclosed United Arab Emirates (UAE)-based investment platform.
What happened? MTN disclosed the partnership in its interim results for the six months ended June 30, 2026. Africa Data Hub will combine MTN’s footprint and local market knowledge with international funding and data centre expertise. MTN has identified South Africa and Nigeria as its priority markets for the data-centre and AI-infrastructure push. Nigeria has Africa’s largest mobile market, while South Africa is a key regional technology and enterprise market.
MTN has already started laying the concrete. In 2025, MTN Nigeria opened the first phase of its 9MW Sifiso Dabengwa Data Centre in Lagos, Nigeria. That first phase delivered 4.5MW of capacity; the full facility is being built in two stages. In South Africa, MTN operates facilities in Centurion, Randburg, Cape Town, and Mtunzini. The Mtunzini site connects to 2Africa, a subsea cable system that carries internet traffic between Africa, Europe, and Asia.
Explain like I’m new here: The new company is the latest step in a plan MTN began outlining with its 2025 full-year results, when it said its Digital Infrastructure business was preparing an AI-enabled data-centre network. The group then opened the first phase of the Lagos facility, and in March 2026, invested in ORAN Development Corporation (ODC), a US technology company developing systems that turn mobile-network sites into computing hubs.Africa Data Hub gives it a vehicle to sell more of the computing and storage happening at the other end.
Between the lines: MTN is looking to turn its telecom footprint into a broader digital infrastructure business. The strategy goes beyond traditional data centres: in March, its Digital Infrastructure arm joined ODC’s $45 million Series A round, which is developing technology to turn mobile sites into distributed computing hubs. The new holding company and the ODC investment point in the same direction: MTN wants to capture the spending that follows Africa’s digitisation, not just the connectivity that enables it.
Zoom out: Africa’s AI opportunity will depend on unglamorous infrastructure: reliable power, fibre, data centres, and enough computing capacity to keep applications running. MTN already has the customers, licences, and physical footprint. The next test is whether it can turn those advantages into a data centre business without losing focus on the telecom markets funding its expansion.
Moonshot is back!
Moonshot 2026 is coming! Join us at the National Theatre, Lagos on October 28 & 29 for two days of tech and innovation. Grab your early bird tickets now and get 15% off.
Regulation
Kenya’s gambling regulator can now collect the fees it was told to stop collecting
Kenya’s gambling industry has spent the past month in a regulatory limbo. The government said it needed new rules to clean up the sector, operators said some of those rules were too expensive, and the courts have been stuck in the middle.
Now, the regulator has won a temporary round.
What happened? Kenya’s High Court has ruled that the Gambling Regulatory Authority of Kenya (GRAK), the regulator that licences and supervises gambling businesses, can resume collecting disputed licencing fees while a case challenging the country’s new gambling rules continues. The decision reverses an earlier order that had stopped the fees from being implemented.
Explain like I’m new here: Kenya overhauled its gambling laws with the Gambling Control Act, 2025, which replaced the old Betting, Lotteries, and Gaming Act that GRAK created. The detailed licencing regulations came into effect in June 2026, setting out licence categories, application procedures, financial requirements, and renewal rules.
Between the lines: An online bookmaker licence rose from KES 200,000 ($1,545) to KES 50 million ($387,000), while a casino licence increased from KES 7 million ($54,000) to KES 120 million ($930,000). Operators and other petitioners, including lawyers Thomas Buckley Opar Owuor and Ken Brance, challenged the rules in court, arguing that they were unlawful and that the government had not followed the proper process in making them.
On August 7, the High Court suspended the new licence fees and capital requirements for gambling operators, while allowing most of the other rules to remain in force.
What’s changed now? GRAK went back to court because the suspension created a practical problem: 246 licence applications were stuck. After all, the authority could not complete licencing without collecting the prescribed fees. The court has now allowed GRAK to collect those fees while the main case is still being decided. GRAK has also promised that if the court eventually rules that the fees or regulations were unlawful, it will refund the money collected.
What happens to the gambling industry? Operators can now pay the disputed fees and get licenced, but the fight is not over. The petitioners want the court to cancel the new rules, arguing that the higher fees could push some operators to cut back or leave the market. The case returns on September 21.
Economy
Kenya wants to make its Uganda border crossings harder to game
At Kenya’s western border, customs officials are collecting more money while smugglers are still finding the cheaper route. Lawmakers now want the government to close that gap by aligning taxes with neighbouring countries and upgrading surveillance at the Busia and Malaba Kenyan-Ugandan border crossings.
What happened? At Malaba, there’s a very lucrative road that governments would prefer everyone to use. Kenya’s main road-freight gateway into Uganda collected KES11.04 billion ($85.28 million) in customs revenue in the year ended June 2026, beating its KES10.62 billion ($82 million) target. About 2,200 trucks pass through the crossing every day, carrying everything from fuel to food and manufactured goods.
The problem is that traders are taking shortcuts. Customs and border officials told Kenya’s National Assembly that goods still move through unofficial routes around the border, allowing businesses to dodge customs charges. That leaves traders who follow the rules paying more while their competitors find cheaper ways around the system.
The committee wants East African Community (EAC) countries to narrow their tax differences, which could make smuggling less attractive as a business decision. It also wants more drones and better scanners watching the areas around official crossings.
When doing things by the book becomes expensive enough, someone will always start looking for a back road.
Explain like I’m new here: The committee’s recommendations follow an inspection of Busia and Malaba, where officials saw two problems feeding each other. The crossings are handling more freight, but the holding yard is too small, causing delays and congestion. At the same time, tax differences between Kenya and Uganda can make it cheaper to move goods through unofficial routes. So even as Kenya collects more at the formal border, some traders still have a financial reason to avoid it.
Zoom out: Kenya is trying to solve two border problems at once: stop goods from slipping around the official system and make that system less painful for businesses that use it. Drones and scanners can help catch undeclared cargo, but they may not fix the smuggling headache. Until the tax gap narrows and trucks can cross without losing hours to congestion, that unofficial road will keep looking tempting to anyone with a calculator.
