articles.title: Por que o Sol tem quase toda a massa do Sistema Solar
articles.text:
O Sol é responsável por 99,8% de toda a massa do Sistema Solar. Alguns levantamentos da NASA chegam a 99,86%, porque a massa de poeira, cometas e asteroides menores nunca é conhecida com precisão total. De qualquer forma, sobra menos de 0,2% para todo o resto.
Esse resto inclui os oito planetas, mais de 200 luas, milhões de asteroides e cometas, e todo o gás e poeira espalhados entre eles. Desse pouco que sobra, Júpiter fica com a fatia mais generosa: cerca de 71% de tudo o que não é o Sol.
Depois de Júpiter, o segundo maior pedaço vai para Saturno, seguido por Netuno e Urano. Juntos, os quatro planetas gigantes concentram quase toda a massa que não está no Sol. Os quatro planetas rochosos do Sistema Solar interno — Mercúrio, Vênus, Terra e Marte — mal aparecem na conta.
Imagine um pacote de farinha de um quilo
Para visualizar essa proporção, imagine um pacote de farinha de um quilo representando toda a massa do Sistema Solar. O Sol ocuparia quase o pacote inteiro, cerca de 998 gramas. Sobrariam pouco mais de um grama de farinha para tudo o mais: os sete outros planetas, todas as luas, os asteroides, os cometas e a poeira espalhada entre eles.
Desse grama e pouco restante, Júpiter sozinho levaria quase o grama inteiro, uma pitada generosa. Aos outros planetas, incluindo a Terra, sobrariam poucas migalhas: a Terra equivaleria a menos de três miligramas de farinha, uma fração menor que um grão de sal fino.
A comparação usa números redondos, mas a proporção real é parecida. O Sol tem cerca de 333 mil vezes a massa da Terra e 1.047 vezes a massa de Júpiter, segundo dados da NASA. Júpiter, por sua vez, tem cerca de 318 vezes a massa da Terra.
Por que a massa manda na órbita de tudo
Massa é a quantidade de matéria de um objeto, e ela determina a força da gravidade que esse objeto exerce sobre o que está ao redor. Quanto mais massa, mais forte a atração. Como o Sol concentra quase toda a massa do sistema, sua gravidade domina todo o resto. É por isso que os planetas orbitam o Sol, e não o contrário, mesmo a milhões de quilômetros de distância.
Esse princípio vem da lei da gravitação universal, descrita por Isaac Newton no século XVII e refinada por Albert Einstein na teoria da relatividade geral, dois séculos depois. É consenso da física: quanto maior a diferença de massa entre dois corpos, mais o menor deles fica refém da órbita do maior.
Essa distribuição também explica a própria formação do Sistema Solar, há 4,6 bilhões de anos. Quando a nuvem de gás e poeira que deu origem a tudo colapsou sob o efeito da própria gravidade, a maior parte do material foi parar no centro, formando o Sol. Os planetas se formaram depois, a partir das sobras em órbita.
No Brasil, o Laboratório Nacional de Astrofísica (LNA), em Itajubá (MG), já montou uma versão física dessa desproporção. Em 2013, a instituição espalhou pela cidade um modelo em escala do Sistema Solar, com o Sol representado por uma esfera de 1,5 metro de diâmetro no campus da Universidade Federal de Itajubá (Unifei) e Netuno posicionado a cinco quilômetros dali.
O modelo ajuda a visualizar as distâncias, mas, se fosse construído também em escala de massa, o Sol pesaria toneladas e todos os planetas juntos não passariam de um punhado de areia. Da próxima vez que olhar para o Sol se pondo no horizonte, vale lembrar que aquele disco de luz é, sozinho, quase todo o material que existe entre aqui e a órbita de Netuno.
Rodrigo Mozelli é jornalista formado pela Universidade Metodista de São Paulo (UMESP) e, atualmente, é redator do Olhar Digital.

articles.title: How GM Canada is Steering a Global Mobility Strategy from Ontario | BetaKit
articles.text:
Anyone who has shared a vehicle knows it involves a little compromise. One driver shifts the seat up, while the other moves the mirrors and drops the steering wheel. It can get frustrating, fast.
For engineers at GM Canada, easing that handoff was a technological challenge worth taking on. Within weeks, the Ontario-based team developed code that uses individual key fobs to identify who has unlocked the vehicle and automatically load that person’s profile, including seat and steering wheel positions, favourite music, and saved destinations. After testing the feature for security, privacy, and other requirements, GM rolled it out across a much larger number of vehicles, wherever they are in the world.
“Canada stands at a very enviable point compared with many parts of the world.”
“We have a communication mechanism across our ecosystem to understand customers’ needs, and our teams are continuously working on identifying, innovating, and rolling out solutions,” said Jack Uppal, GM Canada president and managing director, in an interview with Betakit.
Uppal sees the feature as one small example of a broader transformation underway across the automotive industry. Automakers are becoming more like tech companies, using AI and software to expand what vehicles can do and rethink how they’re designed, driven, and improved over time.
Having led teams in China, India, Singapore, and the Middle East, Uppal has watched technology and mobility evolve at different speeds around the world. From that vantage point, he believes Canada has the talent and research strengths to help lead the next era of software-defined vehicles. That potential is backed by considerable industry investment, with automakers’ in-house R&D spending in Canada reaching $898 million in 2024, quadruple the amount spent a decade earlier.
“Canadian engineering talent is absolutely world-class,” he said, pointing to the country’s technical depth, strong academic foundation, and ability to take ideas beyond the lab and apply them to real-world problems at scale.
“Canada stands at a very enviable point compared with many parts of the world,” he said.
From Ontario to the world
More than 1,100 engineers work across GM Canada’s three Ontario campuses. Teams at the Canadian Technical Centres (CTCs) in Markham and Oshawa develop software and run simulations, while the 55-acre McLaughlin Advanced Technology Track allows them to test systems in real vehicles.
But Uppal is clear that they aren’t building solely for the Canadian market. Depending on the project, engineers here may lead testing or simulation, develop a particular layer of technology, or write code from beginning to end. Those innovations can then be incorporated into vehicles across GM’s wider global operations.
Super Cruise offers an example of how far that work can travel.
The hands-free driving technology—considered to be next-gen cruise control—relies on a combination of real-time cameras, radar, GPS, and precision LiDAR-scanned maps to help equipped vehicles steer, adjust their speed, and change lanes on compatible roads. The process was pioneered by engineers in Markham and has now been used to drive more than 1.6 billion kilometres throughout Canada and the US, according to the company. The same mapping approach is now being adapted for Europe, the Middle East, and South Korea, with the needs of each market considered from the start.
“Before we scale it or even pass it on to a single customer, that product would be built to comply with both the regulatory and customer needs in the markets where we want to sell that feature,” noted Uppal.
The Super Cruise system has also continued to evolve as engineers identify new ways drivers want to use it. Uppal pointed to towing as an example of a need that was particularly visible close to home.
“A lot of people, both in Western Canada and just from a lifestyle perspective, are pulling boats and trailers,” he said.
The original technology didn’t account for a trailer’s additional size, weight, and turning radius. Canadian engineers responded by developing a hands-free towing capability, taking it from “identifying the problem, writing the code, testing the code on the roads, and then being able to deploy it across millions of vehicles in North America.”
While Uppal described trailering as “perhaps more of a North American-relevant question,” he said the solution has been “very well received in many other parts of the world.”
Predictive technology and the future of mobility
Developing new features is one thing. Getting them into millions of vehicles quickly and conveniently is another. Over-the-air updates have changed that, allowing automakers to add or improve features after a vehicle is already on the road. GM reports that more than 4.5 million of its vehicles can currently receive these updates, with that number growing by roughly two million each year.
That can save drivers a trip to the service centre. For Uppal, however, it reflects GM’s broader goal of using software to improve both vehicle performance and the experience behind the wheel.
“Moving billions of people around the world is what we’ve done for the last 100 years. It makes me very confident that we’re going to be a company that’s going to move people for another 100 years.”
“We continue to enhance our advanced driver-assistance systems capability,” he said. “For customers, it’s a driving experience that becomes progressively safer, more intuitive, less stressful.”
Looking ahead, Uppal expects vehicles to move beyond simply responding to information in real time.
“We will be moving from a level of real-time computing and really starting to use AI as our footprint into predictive modelling,” he said.
By recognizing patterns and anticipating driving conditions, these systems could help vehicles perform better in snow, stop faster, and respond more effectively in complex traffic. Uppal also sees the potential to save drivers time and reduce congestion. GM’s near-term plans include deeper use of AI, including Gemini, as well as new technology in the next Chevrolet Silverado and GMC Sierra.
That future won’t be limited to electric vehicles, he added, noting GM will continue investing in both EVs and traditional, internal-combustion vehicles as preferences and technologies evolve.
“We’ll be able to meet the customer and meet their needs where they are, and deliver what they need,” he said.
Through those shifts, Uppal expects Canada—which he described as a “big anchor” in GM’s North American software operations—to remain central to the work. For him, the industry may be changing, but the next era builds on what GM has spent the past century doing.
“Moving billions of people around the world is what we’ve done for the last 100 years,” he said. “It makes me very confident that we’re going to be a company that’s going to move people for another 100 years.”

articles.title: Scientists turn DNA into a memory device that uses 100x less power
articles.text:
Scientists turn DNA into a memory device that uses 100x less power
Synthetic DNA was turned into part of a remarkably low-power memory device that could help reshape the future of AI computing.
- Date:
- August 17, 2026
- Source:
- Penn State
- Summary:
- Researchers combined synthetic DNA with a semiconductor to create an ultra-low-power memory device capable of storing and processing information in the same place. The bio-hybrid technology could eventually help make AI systems and next-generation computers far more energy efficient.
- Share:
DNA serves as the genetic blueprint for every living organism, but it is also an extraordinarily dense way to store information. A single gram can hold about 215 million gigabytes of data. Bringing that remarkable storage capacity into electronics could lead to more efficient data centers, faster processing and systems capable of handling increasingly complex information.
The challenge has been finding a way to make biological DNA function effectively alongside electronic materials. Penn State researchers have now developed an approach designed to overcome that incompatibility.
The work, published in Advanced Functional Materials and the subject of a patent application, relies on two key components. One is synthetic DNA, made from commercially available, chemically engineered molecules arranged into short genetic sequences tailored for specific electronic requirements. The other is crystalline perovskite, a semiconductor already used in technologies including solar cells, lasers and data storage devices.
"Biology and electronics are different domains," said Kavya S. Keremane, co-corresponding author and postdoctoral researcher in materials science and engineering at Penn State. "Bridging these two fields required developing an entirely new materials platform that allows them to function seamlessly together. By combining the information storage capabilities of DNA with the exceptional electronic properties of perovskite semiconductors, we created a bio-hybrid system that fundamentally changes how low-power memory devices can be designed."
Building a Low Power Memory Device
Using these materials, the team created a memory resistor, known as a "memristor," that operates with very little energy. Unlike ordinary resistors, which maintain a set resistance to electrical current in devices ranging from cell phones to space shuttles and lose their stored information when power disappears, memristors can preserve a record of previous electrical activity. They can remember the direction in which current previously flowed even after the power source is removed.
That ability allows information to be stored and processed in the same place, resembling the way neurons function in the brain. Such an arrangement could support more simultaneous and sophisticated forms of data processing. According to the researchers, however, practical commercial systems would still require enough storage capacity and electrical power to become costly and inefficient without DNA's ability to pack enormous amounts of information into a very small space while consuming little energy.
"As the demand for artificial intelligence (AI) grows, we need a new strategy for low-power, high-storage devices," said Bed Poudel, co-corresponding author and research professor of materials science and engineering at Penn State.
Poudel said AI and other emerging technologies are expected to depend increasingly on neuromorphic computing, which is designed to operate more like the human brain. Such systems can evaluate multiple inputs at once while making decisions informed by previous experiences and future priorities.
"Usually, it takes more power to store more information. Our device, however, consumes 100 times less power and the storage capacity is higher than traditional storage devices, like flash drives."
Engineering DNA to Conduct Electricity
To construct the device, the researchers added silver nanoparticles to a layer of customized DNA sequences -- specially designed to be of certain compositions and lengths -- that was integrated with thin films of perovskite.
This technique, called "doping," involves introducing a small amount of another material to produce specific properties. In this case, adding the silver nanoparticles allowed the DNA to conduct electricity while also helping its molecular units line up in a more orderly arrangement.
Synthetic DNA offered another important advantage over natural DNA. Unlike natural DNA -- long, entangled strands that behave like wet spaghetti when handled -- short and rigid pieces of synthetic DNA can be arranged with much greater precision at extremely small scales.
According to co-author Neela H. Yennawar, research professor and director of the Penn State Huck Institutes of the Life Sciences' Biomolecular Interactions Core Facility, molecularly engineered DNA can provide structural organization, adjustable electrical conductivity and functional control that natural DNA cannot achieve when incorporated into thin films.
"We can computationally determine exactly which sequences we need and how long they should be, and then we can rationally design them with synthetic DNA," Yennawar said. "These structures can be systematically doped with silver and other ions and engineered to interface seamlessly with perovskites -- transforming DNA from a biological macromolecule into a programmable, multifunctional nanomaterials platform."
DNA and Perovskite Work Better Together
When combined, the silver-doped DNA and perovskite formed bio-hybrid pathways that directed the flow of electrical current through the device.
The researchers found that electrons moved reliably when they applied less than 0.1 volt -- for comparison, standard U.S. outlets have 120 volts -- and the device responded predictably when the direction of the current was changed.
The carefully designed DNA structures, combined with the perovskite, also helped make the device unusually stable. According to the team, it continued operating consistently at temperatures approaching 250 degrees Fahrenheit and remained functional at room temperature for more than six weeks, substantially exceeding the performance standards of existing perovskite-based memory storage devices.
The researchers also reported that the new system could perform the same memory function as comparable technologies while consuming only one-tenth as much power. That level of efficiency could make the approach especially attractive for future electronics designed to handle large amounts of information with lower energy demands.
"Using just the DNA or just perovskite alone did not produce near as robust a result as the combination," Keremane said. "It's this combination that enables a very high memory storage density that requires very little power."
A New Direction for Bio-Inspired Electronics
The team now plans to improve the technology further and explore additional uses for bio-inspired electronic systems.
"Nature has the solution -- we just have to find it and apply it," Poudel said. "This work of integrating DNA into electronics to do amazing things gives a glimpse into what is possible."
In addition to Keremane, Yennawar and Poudel, other Penn State co-authors include co-corresponding author Luyao Zheng, postdoctoral research in materials science and engineering; Haodong Wu, doctoral student in materials science and engineering; Jiamao Zheng, who was a master's student in materials science and engineering at the time of research and has since graduated from Penn State; Shashank Priya, who was a professor of materials science and engineering at the time of research; and Chiranth C. Ravi, who was a master's student in the Huck Institutes of the Life Sciences at the time of research and has since graduated from Penn State. Abhinav Gorthy and co-corresponding author Rashmi Jha, chemical engineering and materials science, University of Minnesota, also contributed.
The U.S. National Science Foundation, the National Institutes of Health, Penn State and the University of Minnesota supported this research.
Story Source:
Materials provided by Penn State. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.

articles.title: WhatsApp está a punto de lanzar una función histórica: adiós a usar Bizum para siempre
articles.text:
Muy pronto, WhatsApp va a implementar uno de los mayores cambios de su historia. La plataforma de mensajería propiedad de Meta está trabajando en una función que va a cambiar por completo la forma en la que usas la app y que va a amenazar el legado de uno de los servicios más populares de nuestro país: Bizum. Pronto llegarán los pagos móviles en WhatsApp a España y otros mercados.
Así lo ha revelado el portal Wabetainfo, especializado en noticias y novedades sobre la aplicación de mensajería instantánea. La citada fuente ha analizado el código fuente de la última versión de WhatsApp y ha encontrado indicios de que la función de pagos en la app permitirá establecer direcciones de facturación en países como Australia, Austria, Canadá, Alemania, Ghana, Italia, España y Estados Unidos.
Esto no confirma que la función de pagos llegará a España, pues la opción de establecer una dirección de facturación puede deberse, simplemente, a la posibilidad de aceptar direcciones para usuarios que residen en países donde los pagos sí están disponibles. No obstante, existe una posibilidad de que el servicio sí esté disponible en estos países en un futuro. Sobre todo si tenemos en cuenta que el nuevo CEO de WhatsApp tiene experiencia en la dirección y desarrollo de plataformas de pagos móviles, lo que aumenta aún más las sospechas de que este servicio (que ya está disponible en algunos mercados) se expanda a más países.
Cómo funcionan los pagos de WhatsApp
Si finalmente los pagos de WhatsApp llegan a España, se convertirán inmediatamente en una alternativa a Bizum, Además, teniendo en cuenta que WhatsApp es la app de mensajería más utilizada del país, la facilidad de uso y la posibilidad de realizar transferencias sin necesidad de salir de la aplicación podría hacer que los pagos de WhatsApp se conviertan en la opción favorita de muchos.
Ahora bien, ¿cómo funcionará esta característica? Tal y como ha dejado ver Wabetainfo, los usuarios podrán activar la función de pagos introduciendo los datos de su tarjeta de crédito o débito, así como su dirección de facturación y otros datos personales. Después, WhatsApp habilitará una sección específica para enviar dinero o incluso realizar pagos en comercios dentro del propio chat de la tienda.
En cualquier caso, el citado medio confirma que todavía es pronto para conocer con exactitud si este servicio llegará a los países mencionados. La función se encuentra en una fase de desarrollo muy temprana y todavía tiene que pasar por diferentes regulaciones.

articles.title: Apple debuts its 'most powerful chip ever' in M5 Ultra and M6 | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Apple announced two new processors on Tuesday, which power its new Mac Mini and Mac Studio models: the M5 Ultra and M6 chips.
The M5 Ultra, which Apple deems its “most powerful chip ever,” fuses two dual-die M5 Max chips to form Apple’s first quad-die chip, designed to manage hefty AI workloads. The chip includes an up-to-36 core CPU and up-to-80 core GPU and 1.2 TB/s of unified memory bandwidth, which is 50% more than the M3 Ultra, which Apple released only about a year and a half ago.
While the M5 Ultra is designed for professionals doing compute-intensive work like complex 3D rendering, visual effects, and running frontier AI models, the Mac Studio with M5 Ultra will no doubt appeal to hobbyist AI developers as well. But Apple’s M6 chip is more geared toward these everyday users, according to the company.
“Built using the cutting-edge 2 nm process, M6 combines a new CPU complex, two additional CPU and GPU cores, a Dual 16-core Neural Engine, and more unified memory bandwidth to power through workloads with amazing energy efficiency,” Apple vice president of Silicon Engineering Sri Santhanam said in a press release.
With the M6’s 12-core CPU complex, which adds two more cores than the M5, the M6 chip can offer nearly a 30% increase in peak GPU compute for AI compared to the M5, which improves the speed of prompt processing when using on-device LLMs.
“With these frameworks and new chips, developers can run and fine-tune large AI models locally on their Mac,” Apple wrote in a press release. “Apple’s developer tools and frameworks automatically optimize performance across the CPU, GPU, and Neural Engine, and give developers the ability to use Apple Foundation Models, App Intents to tap into Apple Intelligence features, or their own proprietary AI models to build and run powerful AI workloads entirely on device.”
Apple trailed behind its competitors when it comes to building its own proprietary AI model — the long-awaited Siri upgrade is powered by Google’s Gemini. But Apple has excelled in using on-device technology to allow users to more securely take advantage of tools like Face ID and Touch ID, which would be a privacy nightmare if processed via the Cloud. Similarly, Apple’s emphasis on powering on-device AI workloads could be where the company has a chance to shine, offering a more secure, controlled environment for developers to experiment with new AI tools.
Apple’s newest Mac Mini devices are available for preorder now, starting at $899. They will ship after September 22.

articles.title: Gamescom Opening Night Live 2026: The biggest announcements and trailers
articles.text:
The Geoff Keighley-hosted Opening Night Live event at Gamescom just wrapped up. Arguably the biggest announcement was the closer: a remastered version of The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt from CD Projekt Red that’s launching in September. But the show also featured a bunch of trailers for others games, including Gears of War: E-Day, Capcom’s upcoming Mega Man sidescroller, and Final Fantasy VII Revelation.
The event took place ahead of a potentially very big fall for the games industry. Grand Theft Auto VI is scheduled to release on November 19th, and the rest of the games industry is largely steering clear of GTA VI’s launch. That means the next several weeks are packed with major releases — and the calendar just got even busier with the Witcher 3 remaster. GTA VI wasn’t shown, but that’s not really a surprise: that game is set to have a reveal event of its own on Thursday.
Here’s our coverage from Gamescom and Opening Night Live. You can watch a replay of the show on YouTube.
- The Witcher 3 is getting a remasterCD Projekt Red is remastering The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt, the hit RPG that first launched in 2015, and the updated game will be available starting September 29th. The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt — Remastered will bring improvements to visuals and combat, a “reimagined” skill tree, and more, and it also includes the first two expansions, Hearts of Stone and Blood and Wine. Remastered will be a free upgrade for players who own the base game on GOG, Steam, Epic Games Store, PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X / S. With the launch of Remastered, The Witcher 3 will also be coming to the Nintendo Switch 2. Read Article >
- Watch out for Weapons.In a new trailer for Final Fantasy VII Revelation, Square Enix showed off footage of the gargantuan Ruby, Emerald, and Ultima Weapons. The game is set to launch in spring 2027 on Nintendo Switch 2, PC, PS5, and Xbox Series X / S.
- The new game from the creator of Inscryption launches next year.Daniel Mullins’ bizarre-looking (complimentary) Pony Island 2: Panda Circus launches on April 27th, 2027. That gives you plenty of time to catch up on the original Pony Island.
- Path of Exile II’s 1.0 launch is set for December 11th.The dungeon crawler launched in early access in December 2024, and the 1.0 version is nearly here. When 1.0 hits, the game will go free to play.
- Building a city brick by brick.Lego Skylines is a new city builder from Cities: Skylines publisher Paradox Interactive, and it seems like it’s got a good mix of traditional city management and that signature Lego whimsy. This is one we at The Verge will be very excited to check out.
- Crazy Taxis.Sega just showed off multiplayer for its Crazy Taxi reboot in a new trailer. It sure looks like Crazy Taxi — which isn’t a bad thing, IMO. The game is set to launch in 2027.
- Mewgenics is coming to PS5, Switch 2, and Xbox Series X / S.The cat-themed strategy roguelike hits consoles on September 8th. It launched on PC earlier this year, and I highly recommend reading our interview with developer Edmund McMillen. Opening Night Live also featured a musical performance of a song from the game. It ruled.
- Proudly made in Ukraine.Ukraine-based 4A Games showed off a short, gritty gameplay trailer for Metro 2039, its latest first-person shooter in the long-running series. It’ll debut February 2027 for the PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X/S, and on PC via Steam and the Epic Games Store. The trailer is age-gated, so you’ll have to click here to view it.
- Agent 47… smoke weed every day.The Doggfather comes to Hitman: World of Assassination. Noted gamer Snoop Dogg is hitting ’em in more ways than one as the next celebrity elusive target in “The Herbalist,” which you can play for free starting August 27th.
- Lots of gameplay from a new D&D game.Unlike Baldur’s Gate 3, Warlock: Dungeons & Dragons is a more action-focused title — as shown in a new trailer, it appears to take inspiration from games like Jedi: Fallen Order and Control. It’s launching in 2027.
- PUBG gets a little edgelord with it.PUBG: Ded.Net is a new multiplayer FPS with roguelite progression… and also a very in-your-face vibe. I love PUBG, but this announcement trailer was a lot to take in. We’ll see if it’s as satisfying to play Ded.Net as it was to get a chicken dinner back in the day.
- The new Control looks out of control.I don’t fully understand what’s happening in Remedy’s Gamescom trailer for Control Resonant, but I do know I want to play it. The game releases on September 24th.
- More Mega Man.Capcom just showed off a new trailer for Mega Man: Dual Override, an upcoming sidescroller in the series. It’s set to launch in 2027. There’s also a silly-looking Mega Man skin coming to Pragmata.
- Crimson Desert is getting an “enhanced” version.The update includes new story moments, voiceovers in more languages, and “all post-launch content to date.” It’s a free update.
- A look at the cast of Silent Hill: Townfall.Following last week’s extended gameplay trailer, we got a briefer look at Silent Hill: Townfall, this time highlighting the game’s cast. It includes Jovan Adepo (3 Body Problem, It: Welcome to Derry), Kezia Burrows (Observation), and Terry O’Quinn (Lost).
- Here’s the story trailer for Gears of War: E-Day.The game, an Xbox console exclusive, launches on October 6th.
- MonHoYoverse.HoYoverse, the developer of games like Genshin Impact and Honkai: Star Rail, is making a new game that looks like a mix of Monster Hunter and Elden Ring. It’s called Nodusfall.
- The new Onimusha’s demo is getting bigger.Capcom is expanding the demo for Onimusha: Way of the Sword with a new location ahead of the full game launch on September 4th. Catch a new trailer on YouTube.
- The Battletoads team is making an art game.An art-themed game, anyway. Murals is an “isometric action-adventure” with a hand-painted style that really captures its messed-up fairy tale vibe. It’s set to launch in 2027.
- RollerCoaster Tycoon is back.Atari just announced that RollerCoaster Tycoon Wonderworks, a new game in the classic theme park simulator franchise, is launching in early access on Steam “soon.” See you at the park.
- GeForce Now is getting support for the Steam ControllerNvidia’s GeForce Now cloud gaming service will officially support Valve’s Steam Controller and Steam Machine starting later this year. With Steam Controller support, you’ll be able to play games with Valve’s great new gamepad when using the GeForce Now app on your Steam Deck or Steam Machine. If you’re using GeForce Now on Windows or macOS, support for the Steam Controller is coming “later,” Nvidia says. GeForce Now is getting a few other upgrades, too. Nvidia will soon add new DLSS 4.5 controls for DLSS Super Resolution, Dynamic Frame Generation, and Ray Reconstruction. (Ray Reconstruction is also officially launching for RTX GPUs in early access.) The previously-announced GOG single sign on is now available. The service will come to more of Amazon’s Fire TV Sticks “later this year,” and you’ll be able to buy a subscription through Amazon. And as of last week, you can officially use GeForce Now on Firefox. Read Article >
- The Witcher 4 developers target a 2028 releaseCD Projekt Red is aiming to launch The Witcher 4 sometime in 2028, joint CEO Michał Nowakowski says in a new video. CD Projekt Red has been working on its next mainline Witcher title for years and has shown videos of it, but now the studio is providing a target release window for when the game might actually come out. There’s more new Witcher to come before The Witcher 4, though. At this week’s Gamescom event, CD Projekt Red will be showing off its upcoming Witcher 3 expansion, Songs of the Past, which is scheduled to release sometime in 2027. Songs of the Past is also set to be part of Gamescom’s Opening Night Live event hosted by Geoff Keighley, which kicks off at 2PM ET on Tuesday. Read Article >

                                                                Redefining Roles For Edge And Cloud AI                                                    
                        The race is on for localized intelligence.
								August 25th, 2026 - 
								By: Ed Sperling
								
							
						
The rapid build-out of AI on the edge marks a fundamental shift in where intelligence is located, how much is included in devices, and the speed at which that intelligence can be applied to everyday problems. While the cloud will still be used for training large language models, the edge will include a collection of smaller, much more targeted language models. Nigel Drego, CTO and co-founder of Quadric, talks about how edge AI will interact with the cloud in co-optimized systems, how the proliferation of edge AI will improve response time and reduce privacy concerns, and how quickly this market is expanding. [According to recent estimates, 100 billion models are being run locally on edge devices today.]

articles.title: Sophie Adenot retourne dans l'espace ce 25 août : pourquoi une EVA dure près de 6 heures, d'ailleurs ?
articles.text:
6h23. La première sortie extravéhiculaire (EVA) de Sophie Adenot aura duré plus longtemps que les deux premiers films du Seigneur des anneaux réunis ! Et la prochaine prévue ce 25 août 2026 devrait être plus ou moins de la même durée.
Cette contrainte de durée a une conséquence très concrète pour la mission en cours. Si Sophie Adenot doit repartir dans le vide ce 25 août, c’est parce que la première sortie du 18 août, menée avec l’Américain Anil Menon, n’a pas permis de terminer toutes les opérations prévues. Une réparation reste à achever sur la Station spatiale internationale (ISS).
D’ailleurs, lorsque l’on regarde l’ensemble des EVA qui se sont déroulées à bord de l’ISS, ces dernières décennies, on se rend compte qu’elles ont toutes plus ou moins la même durée.
Mais pourquoi ? « C’est avant tout fait en fonction du scaphandre, qui a une autonomie de huit heures », précise Nathalie Tinjod, cheffe du projet Histoire de l’Agence spatiale européenne (ESA) : « Cela pose une limite et on essaye d’y insérer le maximum d’opérations. »
La limite du scaphandre des astronautes
Avant de sortir, les astronautes doivent déjà subir une importante préparation. Le temps d’enfiler le scaphandre, mais aussi d’entamer la pré-respiration. Il s’agit d’une opération pour se préparer à la décompression, durant laquelle on leur fait respirer de l’oxygène pur pour éviter que des bulles d’azote ne se forment dans leur sang, ce qui serait extrêmement dangereux durant la sortie. Durant ce laps de temps, ils effectuent aussi certains mouvements pour habituer leurs muscles à ce qu’ils vont accomplir au-dehors.
« Tout cela peut durer entre 20 minutes et 1h30 », ajoute Nathalie Tinjod, « selon le protocole en vigueur ou le type de scaphandre utilisé. » Mais l’idée reste de profiter du temps à l’extérieur permis par le scaphandre, qui dispose de ressources en eau et en oxygène limitées.
Le scaphandre fixe donc une limite haute à ne pas dépasser durant une EVA, et l’importante durée de la préparation demande de s’approcher au maximum de cette limite pour maximiser l’utilité d’une sortie. Cela dit, même avec une capacité à rester dehors plus longtemps, dépasser cette durée pourrait être néfaste pour les astronautes.
« Il faut faire preuve d’humilité »
À l’époque des navettes spatiales, les EVA pouvaient durer plus longtemps. Par exemple, 8 heures et 56 minutes pour James Voss et Susan Helms en 2001, à bord de la navette spatiale Discovery.
Une prouesse aujourd’hui évitée afin de ne pas mettre les astronautes en danger. Au-delà des réserves en eau et en oxygène, les EVA sont très exigeantes physiquement, que ce soit pour se déplacer jusqu’à la zone d’activité ou pour manipuler les différents outils nécessaires au cours de la sortie. Sans parler de difficultés qui peuvent surgir pendant l’intervention.
Et ce, même si ces opérations sont devenues presque routinières avec le temps. Nathalie Tinjod compare cela à la maternité : « C’est quelque chose d’universel et de bien connu, mais aussi complexe et où tout peut mal se passer. Même si c’est la routine, même si l’on maîtrise le tout, il faut faire preuve d’humilité face à un environnement hostile. Le corps humain peut toujours avoir une réaction qui nous échappe. »

articles.title: Noble Audio FoKus Apollo Pro wireless headphones review - luxury design and audio quality - Tech Guide
articles.text:
- RATING
If your idea of luxury is premium sound then the Noble Audio FoKus Apollo Pro Wireless Headphones would be a perfect fit. They are not only luxurious in design but also offer premium audio quality that would impress even the fussiest listeners.
Audiophiles are willing to spend their money to enjoy high quality and that’s exactly what you get with the Noble Audio FoKus Apollo Pro wireless headphones.
And not only do they offer quality audio they also offer design quality as well.
They are available in two colorways: Burgundy and Peacock and have been designed more like a fashion accessory rather than a tech product.
Priced at $999, they are made with a lightweight anodized aluminium frame and feature plush velvet cushioned leather ear pads and a soft headband so not only do they look attractive but it’s also comfortable enough to wear all day.
We received the Burgundy pair for our review and found them comfortable to wear for extended periods, like an international flight.
The leather on the ear cups and headband, the parts of the headphones that touch your head, is soft and luxurious.
The headband is made from Italian Alcantara, which is the same material used for the interior of a super car.
The clamp force is significantly softened thanks to the ear cups so it’s no effort to wear them for hours and hours.
Our only note is that the ear cups could have been slightly bigger.
One difference with the Noble Audio FoKus Apollo Pro wireless headphones is the fact they feature not one but two separate drivers in each ear cup.
One is used to produce bass and mid-range frequencies while the other is solely tuned for treble.
As the saying goes, “many hands make light work” so having extra drivers means they can do their own jobs more effectively and combine to produce a better result than a single driver could manage.
And the result is superb with a rich and warm sound with exceptional detail and clearer vocals that sound real and organic.
The base is deeper yet measured and precise and you can clearly hear the separation between the lows, mids, and highs which are powerful without treading on each other.
The word that comes to mind is balance with the sound coming through the headphones as natural as if you are sitting in front of a stage and listening the performance live.
No matter what type of music you are listening to, the headphones can adjust perfectly to produce a quality of sound that will put a smile to your face and create a real emotional connection.
The physical controls on the headphones are easily accessible so you can navigate your music, control the volume, and easily toggle between active noise cancellation and ambient mode.
Active noise cancellation is impressive and does a great job in blocking the outside world so would be ideal to use on flights and the noisy environments.
Another great feature of the Noble Audio FoKus Apollo Pro wireless headphones is the fact that the system uses a voice tells you when power is on or ANC or ambient mode is engaged rather than just using sounds and beeps.
When it comes to call quality, you’re getting a premium experience thanks to a detachable boom mic that ensures you can be clearly heard even in noisy environments.
It also comes with additional plugs and an in-flight adapter. Also included is a braided 3.5mm cable and a USB-C to USB-C cable so they can still be used even when the battery is depleted.
Noble Audio has also included a smaller carry case which makes it easier to pack for your travels. But we did notice the case is thinner than the cases we’ve seen from other brands.
On the battery side, the headphones offer up to 60 hours of playtime with noise cancelling switched on, and that goes up to 80 hours without it.
The Noble Audio FoKus Apollo Pro wireless headphones are available now at a price of $999.
VERDICT
If your idea of luxury is premium sound then the Noble Audio FoKus Apollo Pro Wireless Headphones would be a perfect fit. They are not only luxurious in design but also offer premium audio quality that would impress even the fussiest listeners.

articles.title: A satellite collects more data than it can send back to Earth. TakeMe2Space has built the tech to process it up in outer space itself
articles.text:
A satellite collects more data than it can send back to Earth. TakeMe2Space has built the tech to process it up in outer space itself
The Hyderabad-based company charges $2 a minute for computing time on its satellites and is now raising funds to build a 50-kilowatt data centre in orbit.
A satellite watching the Earth produces vastly more data than it can transmit. The link to the ground is narrow, the passes over a ground station are short, and most of what the sensor captures is discarded or waits for hours to come down. The bottleneck is not the camera but the pipe.
Processing the data where it is collected changes that. If a satellite can run the analysis on board, what comes down is an answer rather than a raw feed, which is smaller, faster and more useful. Doing that requires computing hardware that survives in orbit, where radiation degrades ordinary electronics.
is building that infrastructure. Founded in Hyderabad by Ronak Kumar Samantray, who previously built the software company NowFloats before it was acquired by Reliance Industries in 2019, it describes itself as building AI-first orbital data centre infrastructure in low Earth orbit.
Two dollars a minute
The commercial product is OrbitLab, which the company describes as a satellite-as-a-service platform. A student, a researcher or a business uploads an AI model to a satellite; it runs there, and the results come back encrypted. Users pay for the computing time they use, at a rate of $2 per minute.
It has flown the capability rather than only described it. In January 2025, it completed a fourteen-day orbital demonstration using ISRO's PSLV Orbital Experiment Module, a platform that repurposes the rocket's spent fourth stage as an orbital testbed. The company says the mission showed it could uplink large AI models from the ground, run external code on a satellite, and downlink encrypted results.
It has approached the radiation problem through materials. It has developed a shielding coating it calls RadShield, which it says survived multiple solar flares in orbit and extended the life of components, allowing standard electronics to be used rather than expensive radiation-hardened parts.
A third product, StarSense, is an AI-powered star tracker, the instrument a spacecraft uses to work out which way it is pointing by reading star patterns. It is backed by IN-SPACe's Technology Adoption Fund, the same scheme that selected Astrobase and SatSure as its first recipients.
Unfortunately, the spacetech startup’s first operational satellite, MOI-1, was destroyed on January 12, 2026, when the PSLV-C62 launch failed. The mission failed due to a third-stage roll-rate anomaly during the ISRO flight. The startup has since scheduled its replacement, MOI-1a, for a tentative launch in October 2026 from California.
Five million dollars, and fifty-five more sought
TakeMe2Space raised $5 million in a seed round announced in January 2026, led by Chiratae Ventures with Unicorn India Ventures, Artha Venture Fund and SeaFund. Total funding stands at about $5.64 million across three rounds. The money is for expanding from one satellite to six, targeting around 5 kilowatts of computing capacity in orbit and connecting the spacecraft with optical links.
Its ambition runs considerably further. Samantray told a space industry publication in April that the company was seeking $55 million to establish a 50-kilowatt orbital data centre, the block size from which a gigawatt facility would be built.
Manufacturing is largely internal. Samantray has said everything that flies on its satellites is designed and built in-house except solar cells and propulsion, which is the basis of its cost claims.
The company has grown from 17 people towards a target of around 60, and plans operations across India, the United States and Australia. In August 2026, it was among the twenty space startups whose founders met the Prime Minister on National Space Day.
What it has not published is a revenue figure, a customer count or how much of its orbital capacity is being used. A platform priced by the minute is only worth what people spend minutes on.
(This story has been researched and compiled using publicly available information.)

articles.title: Ce vélo électrique à 1899 € passe vraiment partout, mais ses 34 kg ne s'oublient pas
articles.text:
Avec deux suspensions, un moteur central de 100 Nm et des fonctions antivol, l'Engwe E26 3.0 Pro veut réunir ville et chemins au sein d'un seul vélo électrique. Nous avons vérifié ce que cet “e-SUV” de 34 kg avait réellement dans les roues.
L'Engwe E26 3.0 Pro appartient à la catégorie des “e-SUV”. Derrière cette appellation empruntée à l'automobile se cache un VTC électrique tout suspendu, conçu pour alterner les trajets quotidiens et les escapades sur les chemins. Il embarque un moteur central de 250 W développant jusqu'à 100 Nm de couple, une batterie amovible de 720 Wh et des pneus de 26 x 3 pouces.
Le vélo est commercialisé à 1899 € au lieu de 2099 € au moment de la rédaction de ce test. Un tarif agressif pour un modèle doté d'une double suspension, de freins hydrauliques et d'une connectivité complète. Les équivalents des marques spécialisées s'avèrent généralement bien plus chers, même si la diversité des équipements rend toute comparaison directe complexe.
L'E26 3.0 Pro est livré largement préassemblé. Il ne reste qu'à fixer la roue et le garde-boue avant, le guidon, la selle et les pédales. Les outils nécessaires sont fournis et les différentes étapes ne présentent pas de difficulté particulière. Engwe recommande néanmoins de procéder à deux, un conseil que nous avons choisi d'ignorer pour les besoins de ce test. Bilan, l’opération demeure réalisable en solo, mais les 34 kg du vélo rendent certaines manipulations assez délicates.
Ce poids constitue effectivement sa principale contrainte. L'E26 3.0 Pro n'est pas un vélo que l'on va monter dans un appartement ni glisser sur un porte-vélos lambda. Son gabarit exige bien plus de précautions que celui de l'Engwe Zip que nous avons testé récemment. Il faudra disposer d'un garage ou local pour le garder et vérifier la capacité de son équipement de transport.
Le cadre ouvert facilite l'enjambement. Engwe recommande son vélo aux cyclistes mesurant de 1,63 à 1,93 m. Cela tombe bien, votre testeur se situe tout juste au niveau de la limite inférieure. La selle et le guidon sont réglables, offrant une position assez droite. L'assise, large et généreusement rembourrée, se prête davantage à la promenade qu'à un pilotage sportif.
Le confort s'appuie sur des pneus larges, une fourche avant de 80 mm et un amortisseur pneumatique arrière. La pression de ce dernier doit être adaptée au poids du cycliste. L'ensemble filtre efficacement les imperfections de la route, les raccords de chaussée et les racines.
L'équipement de série est complet. Le porte-bagages supporte ainsi jusqu'à 25 kg, tandis que les garde-boue enveloppent correctement les deux roues. Une béquille, un feu arrière et un puissant phare avant répondent aussi présent. Sur notre exemplaire, le faisceau du phare était toutefois orienté trop bas. Son emplacement complique d'ailleurs son réglage : le relever demanderait de réorganiser une partie du poste de pilotage. Nous aurions dû anticiper cela avant notre sortie nocturne.
L'écran couleur 3,5 pouces affiche clairement la vitesse, le niveau d'assistance, le pourcentage de batterie et la distance parcourue. Les commandes à gauche servent à allumer le 2-roues, régler l'assistance et activer l'éclairage. À droite, une commande Shimano gère les huit vitesses, bien utiles pour doser l'effort au moment de lancer la machine. À peine un quart de tour de pédale suffit d'ailleurs à enclencher le moteur.
La finition générale inspire confiance. Seul bémol : un léger grincement provenant de la partie supérieure de la fourche ou de la potence. Sans conséquence sur la conduite, le bruit devient néanmoins agaçant sur les chemins irréguliers.
L'E26 3.0 Pro peut fonctionner sans smartphone, mais l'app Engwe ajoute plusieurs fonctions liées au confort et, surtout, à la sécurité. L'association initiale s'avère plus laborieuse qu'elle ne devrait l'être : il faut retirer la batterie, la brancher brièvement au chargeur, placer son interrupteur rouge sur la position prévue, puis la réinstaller avant de lancer l'appairage Bluetooth. L'opération n'est à réaliser qu'une fois, heureusement.
L'écran principal reprend la charge et permet de sélectionner l'assistance, allumer la lumière ou verrouiller le système. Les commandes d'assistance et d'éclairage font doublon avec celles du guidon. Le déverrouillage automatique à proximité du smartphone est en revanche très pratique, car il évite de saisir son code à chaque départ et a fonctionné sans la moindre difficulté.
L'alarme de mouvement et la géolocalisation GPS donnent davantage de sens à cette connectivité. Une fois le vélo verrouillé, l'application peut déclencher une alarme s'il est déplacé. Discrète, elle conserve tout de même un effet dissuasif. La carte indique la position et peut lancer un itinéraire pour le rejoindre. Le service GPS est inclus la première année, puis facturé 39 €/an, sans renouvellement automatique.
Les 34 kg de l'E26 3.0 Pro se font oublier dès que l'assistance entre en action. Son moteur central réagit rapidement à la pression exercée sur les pédales et délivre une poussée franche. Les premiers niveaux suffisent à conserver un rythme tranquille sur le plat. En position 5, le vélo prend rapidement de la vitesse et atteint sans difficulté la limite réglementaire de 25 km/h. L'élan permet ensuite de voir afficher environ 27 km/h au compteur, une fois l'assistance coupée.
Une montée assez prononcée, abordée à la sortie d'un chemin forestier, a ainsi été franchie avec un peu d'élan et le niveau 5 d'assistance, sans réclamer d'effort excessif sur les pédales. Nous n'avons pas pu reproduire l'essai sur notre côte habituelle, plus exigeante, celle-ci étant toujours interdite à la circulation à la suite des incendies dans la région. Ce premier résultat confirme néanmoins que le moteur dispose d'une réserve confortable pour les parcours vallonnés.
Les freins à disque hydrauliques de 180 mm sont à la hauteur. Lancé à pleine vitesse, l'E26 3.0 Pro s'est immobilisé en 4 à 5 m en sollicitant les deux freins. Le freinage s'avère en outre puissant et facile à doser.
Sur les pistes cyclables, l'E26 3.0 Pro se mène aisément malgré son gabarit. Ses pneus assurent une bonne stabilité et permettent de quitter le bitume sans hésitation. Nous avons arpenté des bas-côtés meubles, franchi des racines et emprunté plusieurs chemins forestiers : les deux suspensions et la selle absorbent une grande partie des secousses.
Nous nous sommes aussi aventurés sur la plage et en forêt. Le vélo progresse sans peine sur un sable suffisamment compact, mais ses pneus de 3 pouces ne font pas de miracle dès que les roues s'enfoncent de quelques centimètres. Il devient alors impossible d'avancer en restant assis. Le mode d'assistance à la marche, activé en maintenant le bouton “–”, permet heureusement de dégager plus facilement la machine sans devoir pousser seul ses 34 kg.
Sans assistance, le bilan change radicalement. Sur le plat, il reste possible de faire rouler l'engin, mais son poids et ses larges pneus imposent rapidement un effort important. Rappelons qu'il pèse au moins autant que deux vélos musculaires réunis…
Engwe annonce jusqu'à 135 km d’autonomie avec sa batterie de 720 Wh. Cette valeur est obtenue au premier niveau d'assistance avec un cycliste pesant 75 kg, sur terrain plat et dans des conditions favorables. Elle constitue donc un maximum théorique plutôt qu'une autonomie à espérer au quotidien.
Nous avons parcouru 65 km en utilisant le niveau 5 pendant environ un tiers du trajet et le niveau 3 le reste du temps. À l'arrivée, l'écran affichait encore 17 % de batterie. À ce rythme, parcourir une distance totale de 75 à 80 km paraît tout à fait réaliste, sans vider complètement la batterie. Le résultat s'avère appréciable compte tenu du poids du vélo, ses pneus larges et l'utilisation régulière des niveaux d'assistance élevés.
Les niveaux 1 ou 2 devraient permettre d'aller plus loin, mais il faudra alors y mettre du sien. À partir du niveau 3, on avance pratiquement sans effort musculaire. La batterie peut être rechargée directement sur le vélo ou retirée à l'aide de la clé fournie. Engwe annonce entre 4 et 5 h pour une charge complète.
S'il s'avère imposant et lourd, l'Engwe E26 3.0 Pro compense son manque de maniabilité par un excellent confort dès que les roues s'actionnent. Son moteur réagit rapidement, ses 100 Nm de couple facilitent les relances et montées, tandis que les suspensions et les pneus larges lui permettent de quitter le bitume sans trop se poser de questions. Le freinage puissant et la bonne autonomie renforcent cette polyvalence. L'app mobile n'est pas indispensable, mais son déverrouillage automatique, son alarme et sa géolocalisation apportent une réelle valeur ajoutée. Son gabarit le réserve toutefois aux utilisateurs disposant d'un garage ou d'un local facilement accessible : ce n'est ni un vélo à porter dans les escaliers, ni un véritable VTT destiné aux descentes techniques. Pour les trajets quotidiens, les longues balades et les chemins forestiers, c'est une belle proposition. Un poids lourd, certes, mais qui ne manque pas d'arguments.
3

articles.title: Nintendo bat un record de retraits d'émulateurs, et ça ne change rien au problème
articles.text:
Nintendo vient de signer sa plus grosse opération de retrait d’émulateurs Switch à ce jour, et pourtant, rien ne dit qu’elle aura plus d’effet que les précédentes. En une seule journée, l’entreprise a déposé sept notices DMCA distinctes auprès de GitHub, la plus grande plateforme d’hébergement de code au monde. Résultat, plus de 400 dépôts liés à des émulateurs de la console ont disparu d’un coup. Un chiffre impressionnant, mais qui ne change pas grand-chose à un problème que Nintendo n’est jamais parvenu à éradiquer.
Suyu, la cible principale de la purge
La notice la plus lourde de conséquences vise Suyu, un émulateur apparu juste après l’effondrement de Yuzu en 2024. Le réseau de dépôts liés à ce projet dépassait les 100 entrées, un seuil au-delà duquel GitHub traite l’ensemble de la grappe d’un coup plutôt que dépôt par dépôt. Résultat, 311 dépôts sont tombés en une seule notice, soit plus des trois quarts du total de l’opération.
Les six autres notices ciblaient des projets plus modestes, mais tout aussi variés. Parmi eux, Skyline, un émulateur pour Android que ses développeurs avaient pourtant arrêté de leur plein gré en 2023, perd 29 dépôts. MonoNX, un émulateur écrit en C#, en perd 17. Plusieurs forks de Yuzu complètent la liste, certains ne représentant qu’un seul dépôt principal, d’autres des dizaines de copies dérivées.
Le même argument juridique, encore et encore
Dans les sept notices, Nintendo avance systématiquement le même raisonnement. Selon l’entreprise, ces émulateurs utiliseraient des copies non autorisées des clés de chiffrement protégeant ses jeux pour décrypter des ROMs piratées au moment de l’exécution, ce qui constituerait une violation du DMCA, la loi américaine sur le droit d’auteur.
Pour appuyer sa position, Nintendo cite systématiquement deux précédents. D’abord le règlement à l’amiable conclu en 2024 avec Tropic Haze, la société derrière Yuzu, soldé par 2,4 millions de dollars. Ensuite la condamnation, en octobre dernier, du streamer Jesse Keighin, alias EveryGameGuru, à 17 500 dollars par un tribunal du Colorado. Dans les deux cas, la question de l’émulation elle-même n’a jamais été tranchée sur le fond : le premier est un accord à l’amiable, le second un jugement par défaut rendu après que le streamer a cessé de répondre à la procédure.
GitHub affirme pourtant examiner ces demandes avec attention et préférer laisser le contenu en ligne en cas de doute sur sa légalité. Mais le précédent Yuzu semble avoir rendu ce type de retrait quasi automatique pour la plateforme.
Une bataille sans fin
Tous les projets visés cette semaine avaient, en théorie, déjà été neutralisés par le passé. Yuzu a réglé son litige avec Nintendo début 2024, Ryujinx a fermé ses portes en octobre de la même année. Mais le code source de ces projets continue de circuler, d’être forké et remis en ligne par d’autres développeurs, ce qui les remet régulièrement sur le radar de Nintendo.
Pour l’entreprise japonaise, obtenir la suppression de ces dépôts reste la partie facile. Empêcher le code de réapparaître ailleurs est un tout autre défi, les forks ayant tendance à se multiplier plus vite que les notices ne parviennent à les effacer.

articles.title: „Kein Bericht erzählt die ganze Geschichte“: Wie eine Plattform die Lücke bei der KI-Nutzung schließen will
articles.text:
Was OpenAI, Antropic und Google nicht verraten: Analyse-Plattform erstellt detailliertere KI-Nutzung
Künstliche-Intelligenz-Unternehmen wie Anthropic und OpenAI veröffentlichen regelmäßig Berichte darüber, wie Menschen Produkte wie Claude und ChatGPT nutzen. Laut KI-Forscher:innen geben sie allerdings nur die Daten preis, die wir sehen sollen. „Es gibt keine unabhängige Quelle, die dies bestätigen könnte“, sagt Anka Reuel, Doktorandin der Informatik am Stanford Trustworthy AI Research (STAIR) Lab.
Reuel ist eine der Leiter:innen eines neuen Forschungsprojekts namens „AI Observatory“ (auf Deutsch: KI-Beobachtungsstation), das diese Lücke schließen soll. Die öffentliche Plattform aggregiert und analysiert echte KI-Gespräche mit beliebten Modellen wie Claude und Gemini, die mit Zustimmung der Nutzer:innen aus sieben bestehenden Datensätzen gesammelt wurden. Die „Beobachtungsstation“ soll Forscher:innen und politischen Entscheidungsträger:innen unabhängige Informationsquellen zur Verfügung stellen, um zu beurteilen, wie Menschen generative KI nutzen. Derzeit treffen die Verantwortlichen auf der Grundlage sehr begrenzter Daten weitreichende Entscheidungen über die Vorteile und Risiken der KI, so Reuel.
    
Was die Daten über die KI-Nutzung tatsächlich verraten
Durch die Datenanalyse stellten Forscher:innen von AI Observatory fest, dass sich die KI-Nutzung je nach Modell erheblich unterscheidet und sich im Laufe der Zeit verändert hat. Die Untersuchungen zeigen deutlich mehr sensible Verhaltensweisen auf, als in den Berichten großer KI-Unternehmen erfasst werden, die sich nach eigenen Angaben eher auf den beruflichen als auf den privaten Gebrauch konzentrieren.

articles.title: Quatre puces en une : Apple repousse les limites avec la surpuissante M5 Ultra
articles.text:
Apple a présenté ce 25 août 2026 la M5 Ultra, décrite comme la puce la plus puissante jamais sortie de son histoire. Elle équipe le nouveau Mac Studio et sert surtout à faire tourner de très gros modèles d’intelligence artificielle en local. Pour y arriver, Apple a soudé quatre puces ensemble et poussé la mémoire jusqu’à 512 gigaoctets.
Apple appelle cette technologie UltraFusion. Elle assemble deux puces M5 Max, elles-mêmes déjà doublées, pour former un ensemble de quatre puces, une première dans la série M. Un pont très rapide relie ces morceaux pour qu’ils fonctionnent comme un seul processeur, avec des échanges internes à plus de 4,4 téraoctets par seconde. Sur le papier, ça donne jusqu’à 36 cœurs de processeur et jusqu’à 80 cœurs graphiques, chacun épaulé par un petit accélérateur dédié à l’IA.
L’IA générative crée du contenu en quelques secondes, mais souvent au prix de vos données personnelles. Avec Lumo AI, l’assistant européen de Proton, vos conversations restent 100 % confidentielles.
512 Go de mémoire pour l’IA en local
La mémoire est l’argument le plus fort de la M5 Ultra. La puce gère jusqu’à 512 gigaoctets de mémoire unifiée, avec une bande passante de 1,2 téraoctet par seconde, soit 50 % de plus que la M3 Ultra. Cette mémoire, partagée entre le processeur et la partie graphique, permet de charger d’énormes jeux de données d’un seul bloc. Apple promet ainsi d’exécuter en local des modèles de langage de plusieurs centaines de milliards de paramètres, ceux qui tournent d’habitude dans des centres de données.
La marque planche sur ce problème depuis longtemps, par exemple en rangeant un modèle d’IA géant dans la mémoire flash de l’iPhone. Ici, ces modèles s’exécutent sous macOS 26 Golden Gate, dont la dernière version en bêta affiche déjà des gains de performances notables.
Des promesses calibrées par Apple
Les chiffres méritent quelques réserves. Toutes les comparaisons d’Apple se font contre la M3 Ultra, sa précédente puce de ce calibre, car la génération M4 n’a jamais eu de version Ultra. Face à cette M3 Ultra, Apple annonce un processeur jusqu’à 1,3 fois plus rapide et une puissance graphique dédiée à l’IA jusqu’à 4,5 fois supérieure.
La M5 Ultra ajoute aussi un Neural Engine 32 cœurs et un moteur vidéo taillé pour le ProRes et l’AV1. Ces gains viennent des tests maison d’Apple, et le « jusqu’à » rappelle que seules les configurations les mieux dotées atteignent ces sommets.
La M5 Ultra ne s’adresse pas au grand public. Elle vise les métiers du montage vidéo, des effets visuels, du calcul scientifique et ceux qui veulent faire tourner de gros modèles d’IA sans quitter leur bureau. Pour le reste, la puce M6 lancée le même jour suffira largement au quotidien.

articles.title: Cómo solicitar y descargar un informe de toda la cuenta de WhatsApp: ellos saben mucho de ti
articles.text:
WhatsApp permite a cada usuario solicitar un informe detallado sobre los datos y ajustes de su cuenta, una función clave para quienes desean conocer y gestionar la información asociada a su perfil. En un panorama donde la privacidad digital adquiere cada vez más importancia, saber cómo acceder a este reporte se convierte en una herramienta útil y sencilla.
Solicitar el informe de tu cuenta de WhatsApp no requiere conocimientos técnicos avanzados ni aplicaciones externas. Se trata de un procedimiento accesible desde la propia app, pensado para ofrecer transparencia y control sobre los datos recopilados por la plataforma.
PUBLICIDAD
¿Qué contiene el informe de cuenta de WhatsApp?
El informe incluye datos relevantes como la información de perfil, los números de teléfono vinculados, los dispositivos activos y los ajustes de privacidad y seguridad. No aparecen los mensajes, archivos multimedia, ni información de canales o anuncios. El objetivo es que el usuario tenga acceso a su configuración y a los detalles de su cuenta sin exponer el contenido privado de las conversaciones.
Requisitos previos y consideraciones:
- El informe solo puede solicitarse desde la aplicación móvil o WhatsApp Web, no desde las versiones para Windows o Mac.
- Si cambias el número de teléfono, eliminas la cuenta o desinstalas la aplicación antes de que el informe esté listo, se anulará la solicitud y deberás pedirlo de nuevo.
- Una vez enviada la petición, no es posible cancelarla ni modificarla.
Paso a paso: cómo solicitar el informe
- Abre WhatsApp en tu dispositivo principal (móvil o web).
- Dirígete a Ajustes y selecciona Cuenta.
- Elige la opción Solicitar info. de mi cuenta.
- Presiona Solicitar informe. Verás en pantalla la notificación “Solicitud enviada”.
- WhatsApp te indicará la fecha estimada en la que el informe estará disponible, generalmente dentro de tres días.
Si activas la opción de creación automática, recibirás un informe cada mes sin necesidad de repetir el proceso.
Activar y desactivar la creación automática de informes
- Para activar: En el menú Solicitar info. de mi cuenta, activa la opción Crear informes automáticamente. Así, WhatsApp generará un nuevo informe mensual hasta que decidas desactivar la función.
- Para desactivar: En el mismo menú, apaga la opción Crear informes automáticamente. No se generarán nuevos informes hasta que la vuelvas a activar.
Recuerda que si eliminas WhatsApp o cambias de número, perderás la configuración de informes automáticos.
Descargar y exportar el informe
Cuando el informe esté listo, recibirás una notificación en WhatsApp: “El informe de tu cuenta ya está disponible”. Para descargarlo:
- Ve de nuevo a Ajustes > Cuenta > Solicitar info. de mi cuenta.
- Toca Descargar informe. Se descargará un archivo comprimido ZIP en tu teléfono, que incluye archivos HTML y JSON con la información.
- Para guardar o enviar el informe, selecciona Exportar informe y elige la aplicación externa (como correo electrónico, almacenamiento en la nube, etc.).
El informe descargado no puede visualizarse directamente en WhatsApp, pero sí desde cualquier visor compatible con archivos HTML o JSON.
Eliminar el informe de tu dispositivo
Por seguridad, una vez que ya no necesites el informe, puedes eliminar la copia descargada:
- Toca Eliminar informe en la sección Solicitar info. de mi cuenta.
- También puedes borrar el archivo ZIP directamente desde el almacenamiento de tu dispositivo.
Eliminar el informe no afecta en nada a los datos reales de tu cuenta de WhatsApp, solo elimina la copia local del reporte.
Consejos de privacidad y seguridad
Una vez descargado el informe de tu cuenta de WhatsApp, es importante extremar las precauciones para proteger tu información personal. El archivo ZIP contiene datos sensibles sobre tu perfil y configuración, por lo que no se recomienda compartirlo con terceros bajo ninguna circunstancia. Mantener la confidencialidad del informe es fundamental para evitar accesos no autorizados o posibles usos indebidos.
PUBLICIDAD
Si decides guardar una copia del informe fuera de tu teléfono, como en servicios de almacenamiento en la nube o en tu ordenador, utiliza siempre contraseñas robustas y verifica que el acceso esté restringido únicamente a personas de confianza.
La función de informe de cuenta en WhatsApp representa una herramienta útil para el control y la transparencia sobre tus datos. Permite conocer y gestionar la información que la plataforma almacena, dándote mayor autonomía para decidir cómo proteger y manejar tu privacidad digital.

articles.title: Cerebras Talks Going Rack-Scale with Their WSEs at Hot Chips 2026
articles.text:
Following last week’s announcement of their WSE-3 Turbo accelerators and CS-4 racks, Cerebras has come to this year’s Hot Chips conference to present the hardware to the event’s technical crowd. Designed to be a turning point for Cerebras, the CS-4 marks their first foray into a dedicated rack-scale system that can operate inside of a single scale-up domain – giving Cerebras’s hardware the scale it needs to compete with other recent innovations in this space. At the heart of these racks is the turbo version of the WSE-3 wafer scale engine, which has doubled the clockspeeds (and thus performance) of its predecessor essentially across the board.
This article is being written live from the presentation, so please excuse any typos.
Cerebras Talks Going Rack-Scale with Their WSEs at Hot Chips 2026
The development of a rack-scale system is important for Cerebras for several reasons. Besides the sheer performance that a single rack-scale system can offer by putting 3 WSEs within a single rack, the Nexus platform the CS-4 rack is based on is essentially the hardware backbone of Cerebras’s systems for the next few years. As well, this is the next step towards meshing WSEs with GPU racks to play off the strengths of the two accelerator types – in this case, building off of WSEs’ high decode performance. Cerebras is already in the process of this, which will see WSEs paired with AMD’s forthcoming Instinct MI455X accelerators.
Cerebras is diving right in to the subject of the CS-4 rack and the WSE-3T processors/engines inside of the rack-scale system.
CS-4 is designed to push the frontier on both a throughput and energy efficiency basis. Versus CS-3, CS-4 offers 2x more tokens, at 10x more tokens per watt.
A big part of Cerebras’s messaging is on how their wafer scale engines compare to GPUs.
CS-4, in turn, is designed to extend that even further, moving that to upwards of 30x faster than a GPU.
The number that matters the most for inference performance is memory bandwidth. By relying entirely on on-chip SRAM, WSE3-T offers 43,000 TB/second of memory bandwidth
For Cerebras’s rack-scale platform, the company has developed their Nexus platform. The power goes in the front of the Nexus, while the compute goes into the rear in the form of pluggable backpacks.
Diving a bit deeper into the backpacks, the purpose of the backpacks is multi-faceted. Besides providing I/O connectivity to the rack, it also is how power and cooling is attached as well. The CS-4 backpack offers twice the power and cooling as the CS-3 design. At the same time, Cerebras is able to build this with 50% fewer components than CS-3.
Once again making a GPU comparison here, Cerebras is talking about how power delivery works on GPUs. And specifically, what they see as the downsides to the power delivery requirements for these chips.
For CS-4, on the other hand, makes several changes to more efficiently deliver power. The vertical design is a big part of this, as it allows for the DC-DC converters to be very, very close to the busbar.
And the WSEs, effectively stacked on top of these, are also positioned very close, minimizing resistive losses.
Meanwhile the next-gen wafer I/O interface uses a new module structure.
As noted earlier, the backpacks are also how the WSEs are cooled, and connected to the larger liquid cooling network. Each backpack does leak detection and has its own energy meter. As well as being valved for quick disconnects.
Speaking of water, here is a look at how it works on the rack scale.
CS-4 provides power intake from the front of the system. Each PSU is protected by a 30A circuit breaker, with inputs up to 277V AC. There are up to 30 PSU modules installed per backback.
Power is fed from the top of the rack. The AC power delivery system is fully phased balanced.
Meanwhile on the networking/interconnect front, a major point of pride for Cerebras is how their design doesn’t require a large amount of cables. Each wafer routes between its processing elements entirely on the wafer, via the 53PB/sec internal fabric. And even between the wafers of a CS-4, the backpacks connect to each other.
The direct wafer links between the backpacks mean that the wafer-to-wafer latency can be as low as 2 microseconds. There is 2.4Tb/second of aggregate bandwidth from each wafer.
Going over the specs for CS-4, the rack-scale system employs three WSE-3T engines, which offers a total (on paper) improvement of 6x for most throughput and bandwidth metrics.
Taking a quick look at how a model flows through the system with GPT-5.6 SOL. CS-3 is already able to run the world’s largest frontier models. CS-4 will allow for even larger frontier models in the future.
Summing up CS-4, the next-gen rack-scale system is designed to leave even the CS-3 in the dust. The CS-4 will offer both 2x faster tokens and 10x the token capacity on a tokens/second/watt basis.
CS-4 is not Cerebras’s stopping point, either. The Nexus platform is going to be the basis of the CS-5 and CS-6 systems as well, which will employ newer WSEs.
The CS-5 system is due in 2027. Cerebas is promising up to 3 million tokens per megawatt of performance. Or up to 10,000 tokens per second per user.
To support wafer scale processing, everything had to change. 3D packaging, power, and cooling.
And CS-6 will be even more ambitious. Cerebras will be employing DRAM for the first time, stacking DRAM on top of their wafer scale engines to give them ability to design smaller processors with similar memory capacity as the largest WSEs with SRAM. Unfortunately Cerebas is not going into a ton of detail here on just what they are up to, but at a high level the concept appears to be to cut down on the amount of SRAM they have on each WSE in order to pack in a larger amount of compute hardware. That leave the stacked DRAM to pick up the slack in terms of memory.

articles.title: Ir a la playa y volver a casa más cansado que tras un día de trabajo no es extraño: la psicología sabe por qué te pasa
articles.text:
Llegar a la arena, clavar la sombrilla, desplegar la toalla y comenzar a pasar las siguientes horas alternando entre leer, dormir y darse algún chapuzón. En esta situación tan relajante, el esfuerzo físico consciente ha sido prácticamente nulo, pero sin embargo, al llegar a casa es común sentirse agotado como si se acabara de correr un maratón. Y esta sensación de cansancio sin hacer nada físico tiene una explicación.
El cuerpo no para. El principal culpable de este agotamiento en un momento de 'vacaciones' es el estrés térmico. Los humanos somos animales homeotermos, lo que significa que necesitamos mantener una temperatura interna constante para que todos los procesos químicos que ocurren en nuestras células funcionen. Pero cuando nos exponemos al sol en pleno verano, el cuerpo tiene que tratar de refrigerarse a cualquier precio.
Para disipar el calor, el organismo dilata los vasos sanguíneos y bombea más sangre hacia la piel, poniéndonos completamente rojos para poder refrigerarse. Aquí la ciencia apunta a que la exposición al sol aumenta drásticamente la frecuencia cardiaca y la tasa de sudoración, generando síntomas de estrés térmico como mareos o debilidad, incluso cuando el calor ambiental no parece extremo.
Hay más. A esto hay que sumarle el impacto directo del sol en la cabeza, que ha sido analizado por la ciencia y donde se ha demostrado que la radiación solar directa sobre la cabeza y el cuello eleva la temperatura central casi 1ºC y deteriora notablemente el rendimiento cognitivo y motor.
El impacto ocular. Más allá del calor, la propia luz del sol nos cansa, y aquí un estudio japonés de 2004 logró medir objetivamente el desarrollo de la fatiga mental tras la exposición solar. Y los resultados mostraron que el sol induce una fatiga cerebral cuantificable.
El motivo está en la exposición a los rayos ultravioleta, puesto que cuando incluso antes de llegar a quemarnos, nuestro cuerpo activa una respuesta inmune. Aquí hay que tener en cuenta que, si nos quemamos, el daño celular desencadena una respuesta inflamatoria sistémica junto a un aumento de estrés oxidativo. Esto a priori es bastante bueno para protegernos, pero el sistema inmune tiene como problema que consume mucha energía para reparar todos los daños que ocasionan los rayos UV, lo que se traduce en un cansancio generalizado, muy similar a la sensación de cuerpo cortado cuando se está incubando una gripe.
Deshidratación leve. Bajo el sol también es normal perder líquidos de manera constante a través del sudor. Y el problema de esto es que, aunque haya una deshidratación leve, ya es suficiente para alterar el estado de ánimo, mermar la alerta y reducir drásticamente el rendimiento cognitivo.
Esto se explica porque, al haber menos volumen de líquido en la sangre, esta se vuelve ligeramente más espesa, lo que obliga al corazón a trabajar todavía más duro para mantener la presión arterial. Esto se ha visto que afecta a los marcadores neuronales compatibles con fatiga cognitiva derivados del estrés térmico pasivo.
La arena. Por último, pero no menos importante, está el terreno. Si decides dar un paseo por la orilla, ir al chiringuito o simplemente caminar hasta tu toalla, estás consumiendo mucha más energía de lo habitual. Y es que andar sobre la arena requiere casi el doble de energía que hacerlo sobre una superficie firme.
Al ser un terreno irregular y que cede bajo nuestro peso, los músculos y tendones de las piernas (especialmente pantorrillas y tobillos) tienen que hacer un esfuerzo extra de estabilización e impulso. Esto hace que estemos todo el rato haciendo un entrenamiento de resistencia que nos pasa factura junto a todo lo demás.

articles.title: CISA Warns of Exploited Oracle WebLogic Vulnerability
articles.text:
The cybersecurity agency CISA has instructed government organizations to immediately patch a critical vulnerability that has been widely exploited in attacks against Oracle WebLogic servers.
The remote code execution flaw, identified as CVE-2026-21962 with a CVSS score of 10, affects Oracle HTTP Server and the WebLogic Server Proxy plugin, which bridges HTTP Server to WebLogic.
The security hole can be exploited without authentication to hack affected servers. Oracle patched the vulnerability with its January 2026 updates.
CISA added CVE-2026-21962 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog on August 24 and instructed federal agencies to address it by August 27.
[ Read: CISA Tells Federal Agencies to Prioritize Patches Based on Risk ]
While the KEV list is primarily designed for government agencies, all organizations can use it to prioritize patching, alongside other tools and resources.
It’s unclear which attacks triggered CISA’s alert for CVE-2026-21962. The vulnerability has been exploited since January, with the first attacks flagged by CloudSEK.
The security firm warned in March that its honeypots had seen exploitation attempts aimed at Oracle WebLogic servers since January 22, immediately after a PoC exploit was made public.
FalconFeeds mentioned the vulnerability’s exploitation in June, in a post describing the cybercrime supply chain. This was one of the several weaknesses exploited against enterprises, but not specific details were shared.
SOCRadar reported in July that CVE-2026-21962 had been one of the several vulnerabilities exploited by a China-linked threat actor in attacks targeting government infrastructure.
WebLogic servers are often targeted by hackers. CISA’s KEV catalog currently includes more than a dozen such vulnerabilities.
